DataWIKIPASS.strDesc: Pacific Airlines Space Service (PASS) is an interplanetary shuttle service which operates in the Mars/Venus, Mars/Belt, and Luna/Mars transfers. It is the unofficial flag carrier of the Inner System, while its parent company Pacific Airlines is the flag carrier of the Old Philippines. Service: Airline, interplanetary shuttle Country of origin: Old Philippines Key people: Althea Torres (CEO) Parent Company: Pacific Airlines Ticker symbol: IPAC Slogans: Begin brand new in the off world colonies... (on Earth, defunct) Home is one ticket away... (off world, defunct) From sea to sky, we fly

DataWIKIPASSHistory.strDesc:
PASS was established by Pacific Airlines in 2021 to operate the Yunti space elevator. In partnership with Renske Hotel International it opened the Hotel Mare Imbrium on the surface of Luna in 2025. When the colonisation rush led to a historic demand for affordable interplanetary travel, PASS was well placed to service the Inner System, and soon offered a package service which took clients from Earth's major cities all the way to Mars' surface.

The loss of Earth to Kessler Syndrome has upset PASS's hold on the market. Without the steady business of the space elevator, the Earth-Luna-Mars corridor has effectively closed. PASS is in the midst of an aggressive pivot to Mars/Venus and Mars/Belt transfers, though it faces stiff competition from more established services in the region.

DataWIKIPASSMarketing.strDesc: At the Xi Jinping Terminal at Mars, PASS maintain the largest advertising system in the known universe, an enormous screen called the Panascope. At five hundred metres tall by two kilometres wide, it is visible to the human eye from approaching vessels for several hours before the rest of the station, and as such is frequently used as a navigation marker. Besides broadcasting PASS advertising material, it is an advertising venue highly sought after by other corporations. Through rental revenue, the Panascope is expected to recoup its enormous construction costs early next century.

DataWIKIPeacockPictures.strDesc: Peacock Pictures Incorporated is a Xinhuan media studio, production company, and distributor. It is one of the biggest media companies in the System, and a hybrid producer of 'new' and 'old' media. It is most well-known for its feature films, and for its association with a group of directors, actors, and technical directors known as 右岸派, or 'Right Bankers'. Type: Media producer, distributor Alternate names: Kongque Yingye Youxian Gongsi (孔雀影业有限公司) Country of origin: Xinhua, Mars Headquarters: Pavonis Mons Key people: Wei Cheng (president), Di Yaote (chief creative officer) Ticker symbol: PECK Films and Taglines: Those With Loaded Guns 'Take the secret to the grave.' The Disconnect 'Those who know don't talk. And those that talk don't know.' Timelock 'It was just a simple heist. Now it's anything but.' Diamonds in the Rough 'He loved she who loved only money.' Southern Highland 'There's a long long way to fall.'

DataWIKIPeacockPicturesHistory.strDesc:
Peacock Pictures was founded by Xinhua Arts Council to attract filmmakers in Pavonis Mons with the promise of funding assistance and creative freedom. For years the project was deemed a failure by Xinhua representatives, and president Wei Cheng was threatened with removal fourteen times while resisting the influence of her government. In press statements she referred to this period as 'riding the tiger'.

The project's success was gradual rather than overnight. Its growth continued long after becoming profitable. Helping the climb was its growing stable of creative producers, the Right Bank, including directors like Di Yaote and Zhou Feifei, and the acting power couple Benedict Lam and Dalisay. The breakout success of plains thriller Those With Loaded Guns is regarded as Peacock Pictures' watershed moment, and the codification if not the origin of the 'plains' genre.

DataWIKIPeacockPicturesMarketing.strDesc:
The creative freedom of Peacock allowed it license and a budget to do as it pleased, in spite of voices in the Arts Council demanding historical dramas and 'classic science fiction' to compete with the output of the Western studios. Wei Cheng wanted to establish a visual language and a foundation myth for new generations living on Mars. She forced the internal ideological battle into the public eye, where it struck a chord with Martian colonists.

The lives of the creatives are subject to constant tabloid scrutiny, paparazzi, and social media debate. This is encouraged by Peacock, who curate fandoms, inviting audiences into the production process and behind the scenes. The effect is that celebrities seem like close friends of their fans, and in some cases, they are.

DataWIKIRenbao.strDesc: Renbao Smart Technologies Inc. (RST) is an unbordered technology company headquartered in Shenzhen and Suzhou Orbital, with operations in over two hundred countries, off world colonies, and corporate territories. RST's design philosophy is led by the principles of neuromorphology, interconnectivity, and user symbiosis. Its hardware products include the Portal smartphone, the 机 ('Engine' or 'G series') laptop, the 牖 ('Lattice') tablet, and their associated augmented reality peripherals. RST is the leading subsidiary of the Renbao conglomerate. Industry: Consumer electronics Country of origin: Old China Key people: Xu Xiang (CEO), Cheng Xiaoli (CFO), Lai Ying Ho (CDO) Parent Company: Renbao Ticker symbol: REST Slogans: RST. The future's key.

DataWIKIRenbaoHistory.strDesc:
RST was founded in 2027 by Renbao Semiconductor Fabrication at the tail of the 20s fab boom. Its goal was to explore alternative computing architecture in the face of the rising costs of lithographic processes. While designing tests for a system in development, Lai Ying Ho, then a Junior Engineer, developed the predictive-priority-interface as a tool to assist her own work, populating it with surveillance data taken of herself. Her tool was soon in use by her coworkers. Anecdotal accounts have an unknown manager misunderstanding the interface's origin and threatening to fire the entire floor for corporate espionage. When the directors realised the interface could become a mainstream success, they integrated it into their next-generation flagship devices. RST's first major release, the 公式 ('Formula') smartphone, leapfrogged competition, setting industry standards of usability and performance.

RST soon expanded into disparate software and hardware fields such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, high velocity data, cryptography, cybernetics, and wearable technologies. In 2050 Renbao Semiconductor Fabrication restructured itself to refocus the company's mission, renaming itself 'Renbao' and giving RST the remit to pursue its focus on the consumer electronics environment. Renbao was one of the major investors in the construction of Suzhou Orbital, and today monopolises 6% of its interior surface area.

DataWIKISunguraViceroys.strDesc: Sungura Viceroys is a brand of cigarettes manufactured by Sungura Limited, a company from Old Kenya. Viceroys are known for their raw cut and flavour, Sungura's distinctive mascot, and the "Viceroy's orders" gesture associated with their use. Product: Cigarette Manufacturer: Sungura Limited Country of origin: Old Kenya Variants: Viceroy's Menthols, Viceroy's Greens Ticker symbol: SUNG Slogans:Smoke break. Viceroy's orders. For the long burn home. You earned a break.nSweeter than oxygen.

DataWIKISunguraViceroysHistory.strDesc:
The Viceroys brand was created during the Central African States' economic boom in the early colonisation rush. Urbanization and international investment into areas like Nairobi, Kinshasa, and Dar es Salaam created a new suburban working class. Sungura targeted their line of cigarettes at this new market.

Mass emigration from Africa brought Viceroys to space workers and long haul workers. In 2062 the Colonial Trade Commission investigated the popularity of the cigarette among environmental technicians, and a correlation between the cigarette's increasing market share and the rising maintenance costs and failure rates of CO2 scrubbers. The investigation is ongoing, though no action has been taken against Sungura over this issue.

DataWIKISunguraViceroysMarketing.strDesc:
Viceroys' packaging and advertising often feature Sungura's mascot, the eponymous red hare, and the company's cast of stock characters. Though he is portrayed as a trickster, he is good natured and reasonable, and punishes pomposity. His ears form the red V in 'Viceroys' on the cigarette cartons.

The cigarette is filterless and rough. It presents itself as the preferred brand of smokers who want raw flavour after hard shift work. The brand's slogan 'Viceroy's orders' has become common parlance in working communities to mean a smoke break, often accompanied by a V hand gesture and/or thumb over the shoulder.

DataWIKITrenchers.strDesc: Trenchers are a trademarked brand of pre-packaged meals designed for long haul. They require no preparation, cleanup, and are designed to be usable under thrust or in microgravity. Taking after their namesake, most of the packaging is edible, although eating it is considered taboo among space workers. Type: Long life food product Manufacturer: Future Foods Company Country of origin: Old United States Ticker symbol: FUFO Slogans: Hungry enough to eat the table? Almost too easy. You can't say you aren't full. "100% edible."

DataWIKITrenchersHistory.strDesc: Trenchers began as a skunkworks project to deliver maximum nutritional value inside a specific volume and mass, intended for long haul operations. The result was an MRE packet which was itself edible, made of a proprietary digestible fibre. After months of product research, the fibre was dyed white and dubbed StyrofauxmTM.

DataWIKITrenchersMarketing.strDesc:
Astronauts living with thin profit margins and unreliable conditions during the colonisation rush caused a race to the bottom for food staples, which led to the creation of Trenchers. Recognising both the utility and unappealing nature of Trenchers, Future Foods embraced an anti-marketing strategy, portraying their product as a life-saving necessity to be endured rather than enjoyed. A survey conducted by Future Foods revealed that 71% of consumers appreciated honesty in Trenchers' marketing, and that 43% of consumers who bought Trenchers would buy Trenchers again.

A legal dispute over stock prices led to an article in The System Analyst Finance section comically titled "Future Foods' futures feud". The title received over eight thousand complaints.

DataWIKITrenchersSurvivor.strDesc: Trenchers were the subject of media attention during the recovery of an arm of the Nautilus Station lost in the L3 disaster. Synchronisation engineer Radhu Laghari-Paul survived nearly six months trapped inside the arm surviving off Trenchers and grey water. Future Foods exploited a trend where media updates of Laghari-Paul's status coincided with spikes in demand for Trenchers System-wide.

DataWIKITripura.strDesc: Tripura is an Indian manufacturer and distributer of tea that has been in continuous operation for over two hundred years. Product: Tea Manufacturer: Tripura Tea Incorporated Country of origin: Old India Variants: Tripura Breakfast Tea, Tripura Ceremonial Tea, Tripura Cleansing Blend Produced in: Old India, Xinhua, Mars Ticker symbol: TRIP Slogans: Discover bliss Tea brewed with love

DataWIKITripuraHistory.strDesc:
Tripura was established by the British Raj before the First Opium War. Afraid of losing access to China's tea supply, the British began growing tea in India, attempting to break the Qing dynasty's monopoly. When the outcome of the First Opium War proved favourable for Britain, many tea growers including those in the isolated state of Tripura were all-but forgotten. In the 20th century the ownership of Tripura Tea passed to an Indian family for the first time in its history.

Border tension with Old Bangladesh in the 2030s convinced Tripura's Board of Directors of the need to relocate operations outside India. In partnership with ISRO, India's space agency, Tripura bought a stake in the Mangalyaan 7 voyage to Mars. They were allocated 100kg of the voyage's payload which Tripura used to send seed stock and scientific equipment. The expedition's botanists confirmed that with minor alteration tea leaves would grow in Mars' soil.

DataWIKITripuraMarketing.strDesc: All Tripura packaging is rendered with the goddess Tripura Sundari in metallic leaf against Sri Nagara, the city of the mother's residence, painted in the Kalamkari style. Viewed through an augmented reality lens, the 2D renderings become windows into deep, evolving landscapes which change with each viewing, created by the artist known as Macchar. According to the artist, one may stroll endlessly through the streets of Sri Nagara, toward but without ever quite reaching the city centre, where the mother dwells.

DataWIKITripuraVision.strDesc: Common Branding: Brewed with 100% natural ingredients and love, our teas bring you to a higher plane of CONSCIOUSNESS and WELL-BEING with every cup :) Each hand-picked tea blossom is the result of hours of CARE and ATTENTION by our venerable growers :) So you know that when you buy from TRIPURA you are buying PEACE OF MIND TRIPURA: There are THREE CITIES of God's creation. The PHYSICAL, the ASTRAL, and the CAUSAL. SUNDARI: BEAUTY without parallel. TRIPURA SUNDARI is the GREAT COSMIC WISDOM who manifests the fundamental aspects of DIVINITY. She is with you while you WAKE, when you DREAM, when you SLEEP WITHOUT DREAMING. Whether you drink Tripura for a PURE MIND or PEACEFUL SLEEP, you enter a COMMUNE with the SUPREME BEAUTY OF PURE PERCEPTION

DataWIKIUbiqMobile.strDesc: Ubiq Mobile is a telecommunications company and Wireless Internet Service Provider (WISP) which provides internet services for colonies and corporate territories across the Inner System. Its core product is the 'grid', the manufacture and maintenance of hundreds of thousands of dedicated network nodes which form the backbone of a network topology. Because of their mass produced regularity, Ubiq refers to its nodes as the 'Joe Chip'. Service: WISP Origin: Mars Slogan: We're your everywhere

DataWIKIUbiqMobileRole.strDesc:
Ubiq Mobile, and large WISPs generally, sit beside and above the base layer of point to point communications and ad-hoc mesh networks, and below the regional or interplanetary services like Olympus Networks. Compared with the first mesh networks of the colonisation rush and early settlements, Ubiq is both liable and reliable, offering contractual guarantees for both security and coverage to network customers.

Following the Tianbian pact, Ubiq refrains from building a competing satellite network across Mars and the Belt, and is forbidden from operating in the Tharsis trunk.

DataWIKIUbiqMobileTechnology.strDesc: Nodes in the grid are processors with a radio transceiver, photovoltaic cell, and battery. The nodes are small, durable, and low mass. When Ubiq detects network congestion, failure, or sees the potential of increased traffic, thousands of nodes are airdropped to carpet the area, either to repopulate or oversaturate the mesh network. In environments where redundancy is key, like spacecraft or mom and pop stations, Ubiq lay cable to supplement the grid.

DataWIKIZhuangzi.strDesc: Zhuangzi Phenomenology is an advanced communications company formed to deliver faster-than-light information transfer speeds to its customers. Zhuangzi's proprietary technology exploits recent developments in quantum entanglement (QE) and the controlled observation of quantum bits (qubits). All attempts by competitors to reverse engineer this functionality have failed. Accordingly, Zhuangzi has a private monopoly on FTL communications. Service: Communications (superluminal) Origin: Henan Station Parent Company: Zhuangzi Ticker symbol: ZHZI Slogans: Limitless communication We did the impossible. We're dreaming the inconceivable.

DataWIKIZhuangziHistory.strDesc:
Zhuangzi Phenomenology is a division of Zhuangzi, Xinhua's oldest surviving tech giant.

"The wise man looks into space and does not regard the small as too little, nor the great as too big, for he knows that there is no limit to dimensions."
--Master Zhuang

DataWIKIZhuangziTechnology.strDesc:
Zhuangzi's veil of secrecy around its network's design, and its refusal to publish definitive operational data, has led to public speculation about the capabilities and limitations of the product. According to Claudia Vasconcelos at the High Energy Research Institute of Ganymede, their technology is not 'true' FTL in the sense that it does not appear to break relativity.

For a current-gen node, the bandwidth achieved in a point to point exchange is judged by third-party observers at under 0.5 kb/s, or around 200 words per minute. Higher demand is satisfied by adding additional nodes in parallel.

Transmission rates have been steadily improving since the product's launch, during which a node could deliver around 40wpm. Some theorise that instead of technological innovation, Zhuangzi instead artificially limited their own product, and are slowly ramping up its capacity.

ENCEmbassyServicesOKLGKioskTut.strTooltip: Browse and purchase visa application materials for Nnamdi Azikiwe Station/K-Leg, 1036-Ganymed.

ENCEmbassyServicesOKLGKiosk.strTooltip: Browse and purchase visa application materials for Nnamdi Azikiwe Station/K-Leg, 1036-Ganymed.

ENCEmbassyServicesOKLGOnOKLG.strDesc:
Most sovereignties in the System observe a tiered immigration status, or "strata." Usually ranging from undocumented (illegal) immigrant, up to full citizenship, a person's strata dictates which rights they enjoy with the sovereignty.

Rights can include access to certain areas or services, trade authorization, or even legal protections or permissions.

Such rights are usually conferred by parents through birth (jus sanguinis), and in some cases, by being born in the territory (jus soli).

Obtaining legal status after birth usually involves applying for a visa, and may include getting a sponsor and/or paying a significant fee.

Nnamdi Azikiwe Station/K-Leg offers no legal citizenship, only corporate-sponsored Permanent Residence. Unlike many sovereignties, K-Leg immigration pathways conspicuously lack sponsorship programs (except perhaps to those favored by Harbourmaster Adeyemi personally).

ENCEmbassyServicesOKLGVisaOverwhelmed.strDesc:
Cost: $5,000,000

K-Leg's Gold-tier Investor Class Visa Program targets immigrant entrepreneurs with the skills and potential to build businesses in K-Leg that are innovative, can create profits for the corporation, jobs for K-Leg laborers, and can compete on a System-wide scale.

Most sovereignties in the System observe a tiered immigration status, or "strata." Usually ranging from undocumented (illegal) immigrant, up to full citizenship, a person's strata dictates which rights they enjoy with the sovereignty.

Rights can include access to certain areas or services, trade authorization, or even legal protections or permissions.

Such rights are usually conferred by parents through birth (jus sanguinis), and in some cases, by being born in the territory (jus soli).

Obtaining legal status after birth usually involves applying for a visa, and may include getting a sponsor and/or paying a significant fee.

ENCFerryPickupStart.strDesc:
The Pacific Airlines Space Service shuttle is arriving.

NOTE: Using this shuttle will advance game time, anywhere from minutes to days into the future, depending on the destination and ETA. It is advised that users pay any outstanding ledger entries, check their gig expirations, and secure their ships to port before proceeding.

Your installed Polaris NAV TIME/ZOOM module can be used to preview future positions of unmoored/undocked vessels at ferry arrival time.

Estimated travel time:

ENCFerryPickupAllow.strDesc:
You step board the shuttle, and scan the room for any available seats to strap into.

It's a smallish vessel, and mostly a mix of folks not looking like they're about to step into the void to spin some wrenches. Indies tend to have their own ship, while day laborers use whatever barge their foreman provides that shift.

So what's left here are those crossing the cold void to see a distant friendly face, or attend an on-site. Or maybe they're on the first leg of a longer voyage. The kind of folk who brought some leftovers to eat en route, or a book on their PDA.

You strap-in to avoid delaying them any longer, and the rapid hissing of RCS signals your departure.

ENCFerryPickupAllowTeleport.strDesc: The shuttle arrives at your destination.

ENCFerryPickupCancel.strDesc:
You turn away the PASS vessel, and remain where you are.

Pacific Airlines Space Service policy requires passengers to pay the full voyage fare if PASS vessel service is cancelled at point of boarding.

Customers may cancel before vessel arrival for a nominal cancellation fee.

ENCFerryPickupDeny.strDesc:
Pacific Airlines Space Service policy prohibits passengers who are recently involved in combat from boarding PASS vessels.

Customers are advised to call again for ferry service when all conflicts have been resolved.

ENCFirstDockDerelict.strDesc:
The clamps on your docking ring engage and your hull resonates like a struck gong. While your sensors scan the vessel for data, you close your eyes and imagine the fortune that could await you on the other side.

Perhaps you've found a racing skiff: a nimble vessel with a lightweight hull pushed around by a top-of-the-line RCS package and a four can Miura "Hydra" Intake Regulator. Or maybe you've stumbled on a multi-cabin pleasure yacht: an elite catamaran complete with a full bar and corridors adorned with yards of crimson and cream Van Hummel interiors.

Or maybe it's just a dead freighter. A decades-old Testudo hauler packed with trash and sporting a giant hole where the reactor used to be. This is a junkyard, after all.

ENCFirstDockDerelictContd.strDesc:
Whatever it is, you've got access to it now, and a bit of time before Ayosec security goons harrass you.

If you're a salvager, maybe you'll smash and grab rare parts to fence back at OKLG? Cut out whatever you can quickly for a buck. Or with a license, trade a bit of profit for less pressure and more resale reliability.

If you're a mechanic, you could fix it up. Make it fly. Derelicts go for a discount at the ship broker, and any sweat equity you put into it after you buy it is yours to keep. You could even resell it when you're done for a tidy profit.

Or, if you're an outlaw, you could always just steal it. Sometimes it can feel pretty good to stay one step ahead of Ayotimiwa's corporate security goons, if you're willing to give up docking it at patrolled ports.

ENCFirstDockFlotilla.strDesc:
From the outside, the Flotilla looks like an impossible place: a hodgepodge of dead ships welded together at odd angles, entire hulls recognizable and intact, as if a dark star collapsed and sucked half the Boneyard into a single doomed point.

Inside it's a twisting warren of corridors leading to cabins of varying, vague, and ever shifting purpose. Trash and shadows gather in every corner. Figures dart and huddle and lie in heaps. A distinct melange of odors lend the place an air of the tawdry exotic: food, cigarettes, ozone, urine, perfume.

Apparently it all started with a humble salvage pod and a pissed off spacer. Accounts differ as to whether she was dodging criminals or law enforcement or simple docking fees, but in any case, she flew her little Ryokka TU-77a about three thousand clicks outside of 1036 Ganymed, welded it to the side of a reactor-powered Testudo Myna, and parked there for good.

Her tantrum wouldn't have mattered if it weren't for a clever bit of engineering. She managed to hack together a controller for her RCS package that perfectly mimicked the oblong, years-long orbit of Ganymed. Soon after that, a heavy hitter in the criminal underworld caught wind of a spot outside the prying eyes of Ayotimiwa Security, moved his outfit onboard, and the rest is history. Sordid, bloody, vile history.

Now, years on, the Flotilla has ripened into a refuge for criminals, thieves, freedom fighters, the insane. It's become a catch-all for anyone who refuses to hack it in the dead-end labor grind Ayotimiwa sponsors on OKLG station. There are no cops. No docking fees. A scrap trade for hull parts keeps the economy humming, along with a weapons broker, various drug dealers, and the odd humanitarian.

Still, despite all this, there's something to admire about the Flotilla, and the desperate people aboard it. Unlike OKLG, where everyone has their hand in each other's pocket, the spacers here are bound by something stronger than a contract.

The simple fact is that they share needs that can only be met by relying on one another. The need to eat, the need to sleep, the need to breathe. There's a certain pride to living here, an enduring knowledge that despite the fact that you might get stabbed in the liver, at least you won't die wearing an Ayotimiwa t-shirt.

ENCTutorialBridge.strDesc:
A rush of gas escapes the bridge as you force the door open.

Once upon a time this hot little number ferried Panmen to Qiantangmen, Mars L4 to L5 and back, forty-eight people a pop, all the while rated for just thirty-two. A whole fleet of 'em just like it ran that relay on gas blasts so fine and cheap they were hardly there at all.

But in time, the operation evolves or dies. Mars is coming up in the worlds. Their workhorses turn into old nags, are sent out to pasture, here, in K-LEG, awaiting the tender mercies of a full shipbreaker's crew in an Ayo main bay.

K-LEG receives one ship a week, every week, from anywhere and everywhere in the system. It has for almost fifty years. With a full head of steam, Ayotimiwa can just about process one ship a week. Following exigencies of labor and best laid plans, there are now hundreds of ships in a backlog so long and convoluted that they would never see another human soul, let alone the inside of the breaker's yard.

That's where you come in.

ENCTutorialHallway.strDesc: Player entered the hidden zone to trigger the hallway tutorial.

ENCFirstDockVNCA.strDesc:
For those who have spent their lives in the hollow, darkened corridors of spacecraft far from the warmth of Sol, the Newcal aerostat presents itself as a paradise.

Cosmopolitan crowds meander through a cavernous space warmed by sunlight passing through a seemingly endless stretch of transparent walls and ceilings. Beyond the glass, a stunning array of clouds and caustic atmospheric gasses flash and gather in a shifting ombre of blue, pink, and orange. The internal atmosphere, perfectly calibrated to maximize both human comfort and aerostat buoyancy, encircles you like a warm, dry sheet, and carries within it a subtle aroma of flowers and herbs.

ENCFirstDockVNCAContd.strDesc:
Commissioned by the United States after a series of experimental aerostats failed in design, Newcal was finally finished in 2049, and is the only Venusian aerostat system large enough to be considered a major metropolitan area. While originally a US colony, Newcal officially declared its independence from the Old United States in 2059, after the NCN Stevie Nicks was mistakenly shot down by automated defenses in Earth Low Orbit. The acting government of Newcal continues to claim that at the time of the incident the US command structure was compromised.

The city consists of several modular aerostat regions, including among others a high-end shopping district called San Diego and a new advanced aerostat called Los Angeles, currently under construction and slated to be complete in 2083. Since gaining independence Newcal has advanced into a robust parallel information and service economy driven primarily by influencers seeking corporate sponsorships by visiting shops and restaurants where they advocate their patrons on the social media platform Rin Ren.

ENCFirstDockVLA01.strDesc:
The Los Angeles construction district greets you with rebar, tools, catwalks, and sulfur-tinged haze. LA is the NewCal's newest district awaiting completion and integration into the city aerostat proper.

Of course, as with every corporate project, construction is behind schedule and over budget.

Progress is also hindered by jealous factions from Encantado and Cloudbreak who pay lucratively for illicit deliveries of the new construction tech. They justify the sponsorship of a booming sabotage trade by claiming the tech was all developed from data stolen from the older aerostats in the first place.

With a discarded construction tech ID and a fritzy wall panel, you manage to override the Los Angeles Construction Zone service dock, granting you future direct ship access via comms uplink.

NewCal PD and Air Navy may not like it, but you can now dock directly for easier access and exfiltration.

ENCFirstDockOKLG.strDesc:
The door to K-Leg station slides open and you're greeted by the familiar aroma of station vendor fare: spot prawn stir fry in suya curry, kebab of chicken in a yaji spice rub, Szechuan beef with pink peppercorn. Your head knows that the meat is aquaponic or lab grown or worse, but your heart tells you that anything prepared by human hands is better than Trenchers chow.

Tired looking spacers circulate between the bunks, the refuel kiosk and the breaker yard, moving in and out of the gossamer haze of cigarette smoke that is a permanent fixture on the station. The smokes are Sungara Viceroys, the breaker brand of choice. Folks here will chain-smoke them unfiltered no matter how many times Ayotimiwa execs fine them for overworking the CO2 scrubbers.

Your new ship is waiting in port, not far from the kiosk hub and scrap shops. Once you find it you can finally undock from this rock. If you want to strip ships for salvage, all you need are the hand tools you own. But you'll need a welder to start remodeling and repairing hulls.

Either way, if you're lucky, you can finally start making a living. Something beyond the corporate sponsored ratrace of breaking ships for daily wage. A life you can call your own.

ENCFirstDockOKLG_BIZ.strDesc:
Stepping off the tram at K-Leg's commercial district, the difference is immediately apparent. It's not nicer, but...maybe less worn-out? Like less people come here. Or at least less rough and tumble types.

The main point of interest here is the Port Authority office. A place every captain inevitably becomes familiar with, as they navigate the web of red tape surrounding spaceport operations.

Usually, you'll find at least a few pilots and ship owners slouched in line here, down on their luck, and hoping for a break.

The longer the line, the more likely that the "nice" clerk is on duty today.

ENCFirstDockOKLG_BIZ02.strTitle: Ship Broker, Medical Kiosk, and Colony Embassies
ENCFirstDockOKLG_BIZ02.strDesc: This district also offers spacers with funds to spare plenty of lavish means to part with their windfalls. The Ship Broker offers mortgages on pre-owned vessels as well as derelicts from the Boneyard stock. The Van Buren Self-Care kiosk offers medical products and treatments for acute and chronic ailments. Embassies for distant colonies allow application for permanent resident visas, coveted for tax discounts and improved legal treatment. Unfortunately, the decade since the loss of Earth to the ablative cascade of '59 has rendered colony interaction increasingly rare and informal, and legal status highly coveted, let alone full citizenship. Legal status often confers local benefits such as cargo trade discounts and rights to purchase private housing and docking.
ENCFirstDockOKLG_BIZ02.strTooltip: Learn about Ship Broker, Medical Kiosk, and Colony Embassies

ENCFirstDockOKLG_MES.strDesc:
The red neons cast heavy shadows in the Old Emporium, K-Leg's only leisure district. The OE is a relic of a former world, a portal to the halcyon days of the wildcat Nigerian colony before Earth's ablation cascade gutted the economy. Spacers come here to escape the bureaucratic grind, to imagine a world without bosses, to split a chilled bottle of Bismertnaya even when they can't afford to.

A dozen meters away from the shuttle stop you see a knot of revelers gathered in the warm light of the Mescaform bar. Laughter and conversation float through Mescaform in a melange of English, Mandarin, and even Yoruba. That last one might be a sign Ayo managers are mixing it up with the common folk.

Whatever the language, the warm organics of human voices in close proximity is a welcome departure from the hollow echo of comm chatter.

ENCFirstDockOKLG_MES01.strDesc:
One of the faces in the crowd is The Fixer. They're a known quantity in the station community, K-Leg's portal to a system-wide, ever shifting Black Market whose appetite for used ship parts and other rare salvage can never be sated.

Shouldn't be too hard to get The Fixer talking. Just mention you have something to trade and they're likely to be interested.

ENCFirstDockBCER.strDesc: Coasting into Port Mojave reminds you of a cartoon you once saw of a worm burrowing into an apple. The port is in a deep hole in the face of Ceres, and dozens of ships cling to the bore surface like desperate insects. The blinding glare of the grey regolith disappears as you pass the lip, replaced with the dancing green-red-blue neon of drone advertisement swarms. Disembarked, you take the small intestine of passageways through the docks into the greater colon of passageways that is immigration control. It is all unnervingly tidy and clean. There is no rubbish, and once you start to look, you can’t see anyone littering. They don’t even indulge in habits that lead to litter, like smoking, or eating a hotdog in between gesturing with it for emphasis. Instead, everyone lines up and waits patiently to be processed. Weird. The immigration agents are unusually attentive and polite. Faster than you would’ve ever guessed, you’re outside the terminal’s sliding doors and into more open space than you’ve ever seen in your life. Calico City was carved out of huge natural caves, which were themselves carved by aeons of cryovolcanic ice. Now they’re full of tall (or long?) spindly buildings, steel frames easily defying the vague insistence of gravity. Calico City is a city, perhaps the first you’ve visited to earn the label.

ENCFirstDockBCRS.strDesc: Ring Station's main concourse is an unbroken tube running the edge of the toroid. Every segment was built with the psychoengineering principle of 'time to shop', optimising the interval between your arrival and your money's departure. Planck time, if not quicker. Piercing white LEDs strobe overhead. Humanoid advertisements loom over the crowds, heckling and entreating throngs of cashed up asteroid miners to enter the brothels, buy this weed or that amphetamine, or lose it all on penny stocks. It’s no wonder the station’s travel risk assessment talks, backhanded and sotto voce, about a rising incidence of schizophrenia among frequent visitors.

ENCFirstDockEJDR.strDesc:
Much of Luna's infrastructure was never finished, and was abandoned as business interests left for Mars and the Belt.

Workers walked off excavation sites mid-development, leaving wiring exposed, enormous mining drones idle or even actively digging, processed meals and card games lying in tableaux to gather dust, preserved by vacuum.

Launch facilities might feature two completed launchpads, but a grid of zoning beacons show where another seven were due. A maglev network between Jade Rabbit and prominent settlements was never finished, and major lines end abruptly in half-dug trenches waiting for supporting pylons.

Settlements not connected by the maglev largely failed, leading to economic depression and ghost towns.

ENCFirstDockERTH.strDesc:
You shouldn't be here. The old world died in 2059, as the Kessler Syndrome lit the sky.

While the ablation cascade wreaked havok on humanity off-world, those remaining on the surface have suffered worse. The population here is ambitious, clamoring, and uneasy. Pragmatic scavengers proclaiming a New Earth Ostracon holds answers about what is lost, and what is to come.

ENCFirstDockHQCH.strDesc:
Welcome to Qincheng Station. If you have business with Mercury and Prokofiev Penal Colony, conduct it at Qincheng. If not, be on your way.

Qincheng's existence relies on thriving via stability and maintaining an unruffled status quo, even in the face of scarcity, aging infrastructure, and ever more one-way immigrants bound for the surface. The population here is ambitious, clamoring, and uneasy.

Perhaps in time, visitors will be welcome to participate in more than simply port and trade activities.

ENCFirstDockJATL.strDesc:
Welcome to Atlantis! The submarine colony nestled self-sufficiently under the ice crusts of Europa.

Atlantis supplies the lion's share of the System's water trade, along with research coveted by Voltaire and neutral diplomatic positioning pursued by both the Galilean Confederacy and Titan. The population here is patient and ambitious, plying Europa's mysterious, clamoring, and uneasy oceans.

Perhaps in time, visitors will be welcome to participate in more than simply port and trade activities.

ENCFirstDockJFTS.strDesc:
Welcome one and all to Fort Simpson! The capitol of the brand new capital of the Galilean Confederacy.

Where other colonies have resources, administrative acumen, and earned diplomatic clout, Fort Simpson thrives in spirit and eager optimism. The population here is eager, clamoring, and uneasy.

Perhaps in time, visitors will be welcome to participate in more than simply port and trade activities.

ENCFirstDockJPTN.strDesc:
Welcome to Porto Nuevo Station! The gateway to the Jovian industrial colonies, the many moons and Trojans.

Jupiter originally dominated mineral and gas mining, before the Galilean Confederacy threw the Jovian colonies into revolution against corporate rule. The population here is hard-working, clamoring, and uneasy.

Perhaps in time, visitors will be welcome to participate in more than simply port and trade activities.

ENCFirstDockMHNG.strDesc:
Welcome to Hangzhou! Humanities' finest and grandest achievement. Decades in the making. The first and likely the only Earth-like paradise among the stars.

Hangzhou Orbital offers health and leisure available nowhere else in the System, but as to be expected, immigration is therefore formidable and unflinching.

Perhaps in time, visitors will be welcome to participate in more than simply port and trade activities.

ENCFirstDockMLAB.strDesc:
Welcome to 'The Lab'. If you're looking for anything good, you're in the wrong place. Formerly the overwhelmed Noctis Regional Processing Facility, now a miserable gathering place of humanity unwelcome elsewhere.

Not much catches the eye here, and much offends it.

Perhaps in time, visitors will be welcome to participate in more than simply port and trade activities.

ENCFirstDockMSUZ.strDesc:
Welcome to Suzhou! While still impressive, the underfunded Suzhou Orbital will always pale in comparison to the paradise of its sister orbital Hangzhou.

Suzhou Orbital primarily leases acres and acres of its internal surface area to corporations seeking minimal regulation and oversight such as DND Cola, Renbao Smart Technologies, Inc., and Ogiso's Resgister.

Perhaps in time, visitors will be welcome to participate in more than simply port and trade activities.

ENCFirstDockMTRS.strDesc:
Tharsis Landing welcomes all. The capital of Xinhua culture and the the most populous center of trade and influence System-wide.

You'll find nearly anything money can buy in Tharsis Landing, as well as everything else that comes along with making such dreams possible.

Perhaps in time, visitors will be welcome to participate in more than simply port and trade activities.

ENCFirstDockMVOL.strDesc:
Welcome to Voltaire! Home to Brave New World Corporation's famous Voltaire University and high-tech research facility par excellence.

Voltaire hosts the System's best biomedical labs, and is always seeking science materials (and test subjects) to fuel its production of ever new marvels of modern technology.

Perhaps in time, visitors will be welcome to participate in more than simply port and trade activities.

ENCFirstDockSVIR.strDesc:
Welcome to Virginia! The capital and crowning jewel of American space expansion efforts, forever shining in Saturn's breath-taking orbit.

Virginia thrives on military tech and the most sophisticated and vast shipbuilding operation extant in the System after the ablation cascade severed Old Earth. The population here is ambitious, clamoring, and uneasy.

Perhaps in time, visitors will be welcome to participate in more than simply port and trade activities.

ENCFirstDockVCBR.strDesc:
Welcome to Cloudbreak aerostat! The smallest Venusian aerostat, the active science station Cloudbreak is rather unremarkable compared with its neighbors.

Cloudbreak's population is minimal, and most residents are studious sorts, collaborating to research and develop new sensor technology while studying Venus' atmosphere, climate, and surface.

It's still Venus, so there are plenty of influencers, documentarists, and drama-mongers waiting for Cloudbreak to have its day. One such possibility is brewing factionalism pitting Cloudbreak and Encantado against the more powerful Newcal.

Cloudbreak welcomes any aerostat construction tech you're willing to sell.

ENCFirstDockVENC.strDesc:
Animated conversation and raucous laughter greets you as you step into the Encantado Aerostat, the System's central Brazilian hub. Music seems to emanate from all corners. Complex Samba percussions compete with smooth Bossa Nova melodies, occasionally interrupted by the high reverb of a Tropacalia guitar line. The Spacers here lean and lounge, each appearing perfectly content to be standing exactly where they are.

Despite the fact that the aerostat floats just a few hours journey away from NewCal, Encantado has a life and culture all its own. The social scene here revolves around the Grande Prêmio do Encantado, a high stakes RCS racing league with circuits open to amateurs and professionals alike. The sport's lucrative gambling scene attracts all sorts: mobsters, rich corpos, corrupt LEOs, even infamous faces associated with the Briar Rose pirate syndicate.

The fascinating blend of strong personalities, along with proximity to NewCal readership, has created a robust tabloid journalism industry. Every day new stories are beamed across the system, yellow journalism with scandalous headlines featuring scorned lovers, fiery crashes, and nefarious race fixing schemes. The tabloid's recent obsession has been the disappearance of Camellia Middlemist, a beautiful lounge singer locked in a whirlwind romance with Rex Korin, a three time Grande Prêmio champion.

Most here watch the races from the Sol Vermhelo Lounge, a smoky Bossa Nova bar with wraparound windows overlooking the Grande Prêmio finish line. The lounge includes a racing kiosk where inspired (or sufficiently inebriated) spacers can sign up to try their luck in the amateur leagues. At the stage nearby, an array of stunning talent deliver enchanting vocal performances best enjoyed with a Cachaca and Lime in hand.

ENCFirstDockVORB.strDesc: Welcome to the Venus Orbital Station! While certainly less culturally and economically significant than the Venusian aerostat colonies, VORB thrives as a trade and refueling hub for spacefaring vessels incapable of either entering Venus' thick and volatile atmosphere, or exiting Venus' gravity well.

ENCFirstInstallDerelict.strDesc:
During long shifts spent eviscerating half-dead ships in the Boneyard, you often wondered what it would feel like to do the opposite. Why wrench out the beating heart from a wounded ship when you could just nurse it back to health instead?

The question returns to you as you look around this derelict, now through the eyes of a self-employed spacer. The prospect of finding an answer has you feeling like an uncaged animal. The sound of your breathing repeats in your helmet and grows more eager with every exhalation.

You set to work and your tools resound through the hull all around you. During idle moments it's hard not to consider the consequences of installing and uninstalling parts you don't own. Sure, you're in a junkyard. But it's Ayotimiwa's junkyard. And while they might turn a blind eye to the salvage trade when it suits them, they will bring the hammer down as soon as it doesn't.

That goes double if you happen to make a derelict fly. The standard blocks on a Nav Station are onerous, but far from prohibitive. And clever engineering can take you a long way.

But as soon as trash becomes treasure, you can be certain corporation security won't be far behind. And, if you're not careful, possibly a few years in the brig.

Of course, one upside to Ayo being fueled by blood and profit is that they'll sell anything to anyone for the right price. The Ship Broker Kiosk in the OKLG Commercial district keeps a record of every hunk of junk out here. Including this one. So that's where you'd go if you decided to purchase her proper.

Either way, stealing or buying, it won't be cheap. But freedom never is.

GUIRacingKioskInfo.strTooltip: Displays information about registering for and viewing racing leagues

GUIRacingKioskInfoAllow.strDesc: This kiosk allows you to join leagues and view standings and results of most recent races. Racers complete each race in a league individually and in order. Times are compared for league standings. To start a race: 1. First join a league from the racing kiosk (paying the entry fee). Races proceed in order for that league. Your available options depend on your demonstrated ability. 2. While in a league, use your Comms options from your Nav Station to hail the race's kiosk station (e.g. VENC) and select "RACING". 3. Select either "Start practice" or "Start race" from the Comms option to begin the league's next race. Practice as much as you like, but each race occurs only once per league. The timer does not begin immediately. 4. Fly to the racing waypoints. Pass the Start gate to start your time. 5. Fly between paired gate markers (i.e. 1A and 1B) to progress in the race. Usually gates must be passed in numeric order, but some tracks differ. Earn points by completing races, and racers with the highest points in a league earn prize money.

GUIRacingKioskInfoTypesAllow.strDesc: PointToPoint A rally track. Go from the Start gate, pass through gates in order and end at the last gate. Circuit A full-circuit lap track. Go from the Start gate, through gates in order and end at the start gate (possibly with more than 1 lap) Orientation A freestyle navigation track. Go from the Start gate through all the gates in any order you wish and end by passing through the start gate.

ENCFirstReturnOKLG.strDesc:
As comfortable as it feels to return to the station after scouring the cold boneyard for parts, in the world of semi-legal salvage, finding parts is only half the battle. The rest is selling it.

Station centers are connected by rail, a single car shuttle system that is constantly in a state of disrepair. With a working knowledge of the station and an appetite for risk, you might even find a way to make a living on this rock.

The OKLG economy is a strange beast. There's the corporate sponsored salvage trade, run through the scrap and license kiosks. With the right license you can rent time out in the boneyard and pick parts without being bothered by the AyoSec goons.

The black market is another matter. Industrious scavengers know that if you want a premium price for a rare piece, then you're going to have to find a reliable fence. But it won't be easy gaining their trust.

Lastly, the GigNexus shops out jobs to just about anyone. The work ranges from menial station jobs to high-risk boarding operations. In every case, the faster you work, the more money you'll find.

ENCFirstUndockFees.strDesc:
A slight pang of humiliation rushes through you, as the audible buzzer announces your permission is denied. Unpaid docking fees.

"I'm sure it happens all the time," you assure yourself. Surely they won't assume you were trying to skip town without paying?

In any case, you'll need to pay those fees before you're going anywhere. Either click your money total for the Finances ledger, or use one of the ubiquitous orange station kiosks.

That, or find someone at the Port Authority desk who might just let you slide this one time...

ENCFirstUntime.strDesc:
Fourth shift ends and the change in the atmosphere is unmistakable. Shipbreakers stop sparking their hand torches. Long-armed construction waldos drop their grip and drift away from wrecked hulls. Two clicks out, a cargo hauler cuts its reactor and the entire rig burns down like a cold ember in the dark.

Untime: the closest anyone out here will ever get to a Sabbath. Twenty minutes and fifty-eight glorious seconds welded to the end of shift four, a seemingly insignificant stretch of time remaining like loose change after the rest of the hours are divided, counted and spent.

In the beginning, Untime was merely a quirk of the New Celestial Calendar, a more even way to divide the year now that Humanity had uncoupled itself from Earth and its overwrought lunar calendar. But that was decades ago. These days, Untime is for rest, for conversation, for anything at all that won't turn a buck for the bosses.

As for the managers who choose not to observe this fine tradition? Two weeks ago one of them "fell" from a labor barge and hit every ship on the way down.

ENCLaunchShip.strDesc:
With one last look back at the barracks you've called home all these years, you step through the threshold into your salvage pod. It won't get far on its own, but you know of at least a few derelicts, out there in the K-Leg boneyard, that might be candidates for your next ship.

Start checking the derelicts out, and choose one to make your own.

With one last look back at the barracks you've called home all these years, you step through the threshold into your salvage pod. It won't get far on its own, but you know of at least a few derelicts, out there in the K-Leg boneyard, that might be candidates for your next ship.

ENCPoliceBoard.strDesc: The call comes through the tinny speakers. "This is Utopia Risk Management," says a bored voice on the other side of the airlock. "We are legally boarding you under section 27-2 of the Ayotimiwa Operational License Agreement. Have one of your crew report to the airlock and stand well back with your personal devices set to I.D. display."

ENCPurpleSuit.strTitle: The Purple Jumpsuit of The Mariner
ENCPurpleSuit.strDesc:
People can't stop staring. You walk into a room and the chatter dies down as all eyes are drawn to your body sheathed in radiant periwinkle. It's as if you were The Mariner herself.

It's hard to say where the superstitions about The Mariner and the color purple began. It could be as simple as a last name. Before she was The Mariner, the first person to be murdered in space was Olivia Violet Highsmith. She was by all accounts a cheerful NASA engineer hailing from rural Michigan. It's possible that after her infamous and violent passing, someone clever latched on to that middle name and never let go.

But that doesn't explain what The Mariner is said to look like. It doesn't explain the lavender haze that pumps from the severed O2 tube trailing her body. Nor does it describe the attraction. Mariner Seekers insist, and insist they can prove, that purple increases the likelihood of meeting the ancient specter by tenfold.

Doesn't matter now. The belief has stuck and your lavender jumpsuit proves it. The suit came from a merchandising gimmick sponsored by Damask Rose as part of the marketing campaign for their "Purple Curse" strain. That is, until a series of accidents befell customers wearing them, fueling rumors that Damask had angered the ghost by being so cavalier about her passing.

So what you've got on your hands is a collectors item. Just don't expect anyone to buy you any drinks.

ENCMemoryDumb.strTitle: Clobbered by a Memory of the Dumbest Thing You've Ever Said
ENCMemoryDumb.strDesc:
It arrives without warning: a memory from long ago so embarrassing, so superheated by shame, that it feels like molten metal poured down the center of your back. 

Why did you say that? The question haunts you. You could have said anything, quite literally, and instead you said ... that. You see their face, their eyes, their pained wince.

Your rational mind assures you that they've forgotten by now. Surely they've lost track of that catastrophically stupid thing you said. But the soul is not rational, and memory is not fair, so here it sits: The Dumbest Thing You've Ever Said, the moment as fresh now, years later, as it has ever been.

Wow. It's going to take a couple hours to shake that one off.

ENCMemoryLove.strTitle: Clobbered by a Memory of a Love Now Lost
ENCMemoryLove.strDesc:
You find yourself mulling over their memory again, stretching it out like an aching muscle, returning to a pain you've grown fond of because it is, at the very least, familiar.

It was one of your shortest relationships. Perhaps for that very reason it is the one that endures, the one you miss in the quiet moments.

It's the sense memories that remain, mostly. The sound of their laugh. The softness of their forearm felt beneath your thumb. The scent of them between the ear and the nape of the neck.

It's better to have loved and lost, they say. And in moments like this, when you're adrift and otherwise alone in the cold eternity of space, you believe it to be true.

ENCHeatAyoSecBustedStart.strDesc:
They haul you before an AyoSec magistrate for judgement, leaving your ship and gear behind.

At the hearing, you can beg for just a fine- $15,000 payable in full or installments- or it's off to Azikiwe Brig for a year or three of hard labor.

ENCHeatAyoSecFineEnd.strDesc:
It's almost like they want you to break the rules so they can extract more fines from you.

You sign reams of paperwork in tight cuffs.

It's a prison sentence of another sort. Another weight hanging around your neck.

New $15,000 fine added.

ENCHeatAyoSecFineDebtEnd.strTitle: Plead for a fine (Paid in installments)
ENCHeatAyoSecFineDebtEnd.strDesc:
It's almost like they want you to break the rules so they can lock you deeper in interest payments.

You sign reams of paperwork in tight cuffs.

It's a prison sentence of another sort. Another weight hanging around your neck.

New $15,000 debt added, with payment due each shift.

ENCHeatAyoSecFineFinish.strDesc:
After processing, you are unceremoniously dumped outside the OKLG Security Office. If you weren't docked at station when you were arrested, you may need to use the PASS ferry service (on your PDA) to reach your ship again. Hopefully it's still there.

Time to get back on your feet.

ENCHeatAyoSecPrisonStart.strDesc: You are hauled off to Azikiwe Brig.

ENCHeatAyoSecPrisonEnd.strDesc:
You spend months laboring without wage among outcasts both meek and dangerous. You share a dorm with nearly a hundred other souls, all of you stacked like kindling on triple high bunks.

But even a hell like this is not without opportunity. You hear things. You meet people. You get in a few scrapes, you find a few friends. By the end of your term you've lived a dozen lives and you have all the scars to prove it.

Plus, free room and board. In a certain light, it might all be worth it ...

ENVHeatVenusImmunityStart.strDesc:
After all your work cracking the Camellia Middlemist case, you and the DA might as well be close personal friends. That is made very clear during the pre-trial hearing, when a Very Important Somebody approaches the magistrate during your plea.

 You're let off the hook without another word. Nothing better than having friends in high places.

ENCHackPDAStart.strDesc:
This PDA is locked, and requires authentication to access its contents.

Most PDAs feature a variety of authenticators, including passwords, PINs, and various sensor-based biometrics. But simply brute-forcing through those will be futile due to failed login attempt limits and lock-outs.

If you want to use this device, you'll need to find another way in.

ENCHackPDASkill.strDesc:
Defeating the security on devices like these was always a siren's call. A puzzle you could sink your teeth into in your down time.

And thanks to various governmental authorities, plus the manufacturer's recovery pipeline, each device has multiple backdoors for you to find an exploit. Like a puzzle with multiple solutions!

Anyway, you try to remember the trick to this particular model...

ENCHackPDASkillFinished.strDesc:
Sure enough, nobody bothered to patch the exploit you chose this time, and you're greeted with the home screen.

That's the problem with behemoth orgs: not very nimble. And the hacker community chews through them too fast.

Oh well, at least it was worth the little nostalgia kick.

ENCHackPDASoftwareFail.strDesc:
You launch the cracking program, but it doesn't take long to realize you're in over your head.

What does this software even do? Does it work on devices like these? Do you plug the target device in somewhere? Or do you need to start the software first?

You wish there was a tutorial or something.

Or even some menus.

Oh well, no 1337 h4x0r5 for you.

ENCHackPDASoftwareStart.strDesc: Hacking was never your thing, but you decide to give the PDA a look anyway. Maybe there's a boot menu or something? Safe mode?

ENCHackPDASoftwareLacking.strDesc: After a while of messing with it, you don't really make any headway. And you're out of ideas. Without more hacking skills, you'll probably need an already-unlocked PDA and some sort of software to crack this PDA.

ENCHackPDASoftware.strDesc:
Even without much hacking practice, you know your way around software well enough to use cracking software.

Using your unlocked device to run R3N-B00, you scan for compatible devices, and select your target.

ENCHackPDASoftwareFinished.strDesc:
**** R3N-B00 Cracker ****

Destination device: [them]

Status: UNLOCKED

Have a nice day!
