PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound01.strDesc: [us] wistfully [imagines] tasting real Earth food: grass-fed meat, fresh-caught fish, field-grown produce.

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound02.strDesc: [us] [inspects] [them], indulging in imagining what "mystery meat" really is. A station terminal or food authority would probably know more.

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound03.strDesc: [us] [inspects] [them] closely, removing all visible chunks of "mystery meat" possible to improve the eating experience.

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound04.strDesc: [us] tries looking up info about Trenchers' "Mystery Meat" using [them].

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound04Reply.strDesc:
[them] [finds] info using [them] about Trenchers' parent company being the megacorp Future Foods, famous in recent years for its tongue-twisting "Futures Feud" scandal.
There is understandably not much information about its "mystery meat" product, but there are many questions. Some competitors in the space appear to be Brave New World's bioengineering researchers at Voltaire, Deimos, who have done some work on goats in the past. There is more info out there to find, surely. Maybe hacking skills could find more from more official terminals.

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound04b.strDesc: [us] [asks] [them] for more info about Trenchers' "Mystery Meat".

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound04bReply.strDesc:
[us] [tells] [them] what they've heard about the secrecy maintained by Trenchers' parent company, Future Foods.
They reluctantly indicate that other companies are also working on "mystery meat" products, such as Brave New World's bioengineering researchers at Voltaire, Deimos, Prokofiev Penal Colony on Mercury, or even Hyun Lee Petware. [us-subj] [is] hesitant and superstitious about the topic. There is more to learn, surely.

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound05.strDesc: [us] [watches] [them] more closely to find out more about uber-corp experiments pursuing a supposed infinite source of food.

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound05Reply.strTitle: View News about Perpetual Food Source
PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound05Reply.strDesc: [them] [learns] of a failed bioengineering lab outside of Tharsis Landing on Mars where Brave New World, LLC was experimenting on goats.

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound06.strDesc: [us] [asks] [them] how [them-contractIs] been eating recently. Food scarcity is common among the colonies, especially on crowded stations, and complaining about Trenchers is basically spacer tradition.

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound06ReplyManager.strDesc: [us] happily [shares] with [them] [us-pos] most recent decadent meal. Unlike the rest of humanity, corporate managers often enjoy the gourmet, Earth-like produce from Hangzhou Orbital, or bioengineered food coming out of Voltaire, Deimos.

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound06ReplyHangzhou.strDesc: [us] merrily [recounts] stories for [them] about growing up on Hangzhou Orbital, with its Earth-like conditions, gravity, even lakes and an artificial sunlight cycle. Hangzhou, in orbit around Mars, is one of the few places in the Solar System that doesn't know constant food scarcity.

PLOT_Meat_WhispersFound06Reply.strDesc: [us] [thanks] them for asking and [tells] [them] the perennial story of spacers' rations stretched too thin. Food just doesn't grow well enough in space to feed everybody. They say the Hangzhou Orbital has Earth-like agriculture, but controls supply and gouges the rest of the colonies for its dream food products.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed01.strDesc: [us] [discusses] with [them] about rumored news of corporate experiments in the Martian system seeking infinite food sources.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed02.strDesc: [us] [discusses] with [them] the injustices of spacers' incessant hunger, corporations' role in scarcities, and hopes for technological breakthroughs in food production and distribution.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed03.strDesc: [us] [hacks] the records of various ubercorporations, seeking info about research into infinite food sources.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed03ReplyLEOShip.strDesc: [them] [unearths] some juicy police records via the local authority terminal's access: Highly redacted incident reports about deaths and missing person cases have an unsettling pattern of leading to ships and derelicts reported to be infested with rapidly growing, disembodied, meat. Some reports marked for psychological review even say the meat was possibly breathing, and speaking. There is more to this rabbit trail. But where?

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed03ReplyBIZ.strDesc: [them] [finds] revealing records using the more official access granted by the business terminal: Brave New Worlds LLC has gone to great lengths to quash inquiry into its "Perpetual Protein" project, mostly to avoid bad publicity. Some of its efforts have included smearing the reputation of The Fishers of Men, a religious activist group on Kapyong station, as well as Future Foods Inc, their top competitor. There has to be still more out there.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed03Reply.strDesc: [them] [finds] rumors of investment pitches involving corporate genetic food science experimentation intended to lucratively bolster station and colony nutrition by creating protein from thin air. It seems improbable: the pitches probably went nowhere or were shut down by Xinhua's dominant agricultural ubercorporations. Terminals with more official access would allow more fruitful hacking. There has to be still more out there.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed04.strDesc: [us] [inspects] [them] that once wrapped what appears to be a prototype for a Perpetual Protein Project.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed04Reply.strDesc: Inspecting [us]: Runny globules of fat and blood are left behind on the inside while corporate jargon and miniscule nutrition liability data covers the outside. Unfamiliar branding shows the Brave New World, LLC logo over the Voltaire University skyline silhouetted against a Mars-rise, with a slogan: Don't ask why. Ask 'why don't I have one?'

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed05.strDesc: [us] [looks] closer at what appears to be chunky blood.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed05Reply.strDesc: Inspecting [us]: It is congealed, darker than usual, with a thick viscous texture, and possibly slightly pulsing. It appears neither of human origin, nor healthy.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed06ReplyCultist.strDesc: [us] [devours] every detail [them] [is] willing to provide. [us-subj] [finds] [us-reflexive] drawn to the idea of the weird blood.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed06ReplyAntiGMO.strDesc: [us] [stops] [them] before [them-subj] [finishes]. [us-subj] [renounces] evidence of genetic modification as diabolical, "playing God", and various other pronouncements.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed06ReplyModerate.strDesc: [us] [interprets] [them-pos] story as something to investigate further. Science can find a way to address the needs of humanity.

PLOT_Meat_SignsDiscussed06Reply.strDesc: [us] [shrugs] and [asks] [them] if [us-subj] [looks] like a doctor or scientist.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged01.strDesc: [us] [looks] more closely at [them], trying to make sense of what it is.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged01Reply.strDesc: Inspecting [us]: Raw, pinkish, veiny meat, quivering where it is not hardened by vacuum or radiation. Tufts of brown and gray bristly hair emerge here and there directly from the muscle, viscera, and veins.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged02.strDesc: [us] [inclines] toward the quivering mass to try listening to the strange susurrations that seem to emanate from within it.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged02Reply.strDesc: [them] [hears] [us]: The murmurs sound like longing and certainty, pronouncements bleating about deeper truth, and that which separates good and evil, in many languages simultaneously, and yet in none.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged03.strDesc: [us] [mentions] living meat masses [us-contractHas] seen around, inviting [them-pos] opinion.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged03ReplyCultist.strDesc: [us] [engages] eagerly about the essence and significance of this meat. [us-subj] [asks] if it has spoken to [them] and [us-insists] that coincidence cannot explain its emergence here and now, right?

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged03ReplyAntiGMO.strDesc: [us] [responds] as if [them] is speaking of demons, or worse. Surely, such an abomination should be purged wherever it may be found. [doesn't] [them] agree?

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged03ReplyModerate.strDesc: [us] [expresses] optimism that science could harness something like that into a useful resource. [us-subj] [recommends] harvesting and studying it.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged03Reply.strDesc: [us] [tells] [them] that sounds pretty gross and weird, but [us-subj] [has] heard other people debating similar topics.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged04.strDesc: [us] [speaks] to the meat mass, certain that it is listening.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged04Reply.strDesc: [them] [hears] [us]: If one is bold and pure of heart, [us-subj] may ask and the King without End may give gifts to those deserving.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged05.strDesc: [us] [asks] meekly whether the King without End is willing to grant his good gifts to one such as [us-obj].

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged05Reply.strDesc: [them] [watches] the mass quiver and shiver into separate segments.

PLOT_Meat_MeatEngaged05ReplyNo.strDesc: [us] [pulsates] but does not change. Perhaps the King without End is unwilling at this time. Perhaps later.

ACTMeleeMeat.strDesc: [them] [quivers] woefully and [us] [hears] an angry bleating sound.

ACTRangedMeat.strDesc: [them] [quivers] woefully and [us] [hears] an angry bleating sound.

ACTMeleeMeatCrush.strTooltip: Attempt to subsume a target by expanding into them.

PLOT_Meat_MeatKnown01Reply.strDesc: Inspecting [us]: It's a goat hoof attached to a large, muscular goat leg that exceeds both animal and human proportions. Its hair is matted with gore, off-color blood, and congealed fat.

PLOT_Meat_MeatKnown02Reply.strDesc: Inspecting [us]: It's a large, spiral-ridged goat horn with dark brown and red coloration. It seems to thrum with a sense of infinitude and possibility.

PLOT_Meat_MeatKnown03Reply.strDesc: Inspecting [us]: It's a giant goat eye, complete with horizontal rectangular pupil that seems to track its observer's gaze. It trails stringy nerves and veins from its partial socket bounded by skinless bands of orbicularis oculi muscle.

PLOT_Meat_MeatKnown04.strDesc: [us] [discusses] the items [us-subj] [has] retrieved from within the meat, seeking info about what to do with them.

PLOT_Meat_MeatKnown04ReplyCultist.strDesc:
[us] [raves] about the glorious threshold on which [them] stands. [us-subj] [reveals] whispers of old dictating that the eternal embrace of the Goat Without End can be called by assembling and kneeling at an altar:
Four cloven hooves, standing sentinel as the pillars of the universe, shall bear the weight of enlightenment.
From these, twin unblemished horns, shall ascend, reaching for the heavens.
And, as a guardian of the celestial gates, pierced upon the horns shall rest a vigilant eye, forever observing, spanning the horizon.
Kneel in reverence, O Seeker, and the Goat Without End shall reveal the veiled mysteries.

PLOT_Meat_MeatKnown04ReplyAntiGMO.strDesc:
[us] [responds] with grim seriousness: Know this, the corrupted spawn of hubris that plagues our universe must be cleansed, and the keys to salvation have been laid bare to the true believers.
Assemble four limbs, representing its mobility, two horns to represent its power, and one eye representing its defilement, and stack them like a pyre.
With conviction in thy heart, strike down upon this unholy assembly and watch as righteousness strikes its heart, the infernal corruption withers, and the puppet masters who birthed it tremble.

PLOT_Meat_MeatKnown04ReplyModerate.strDesc:
[us] [says] that to fully exploit this organism's potential, a comprehensive extraction and analysis are required.
From a sample of muscles from four distinct limbs, study the unique cellular metabolism mechanisms. Extract keratin and growth factors from at least two horns, which likely regulate and support enhanced metabolic processes in the absence of skeletal structure. From the eye, extract the photoreceptive retinal compounds, potentially acting as a light-driven catalyst for rapid growth. By synthesizing these principles and intact physical components, we may unlock safe means to harness an endless, regenerative food supply.

PLOT_Meat_MeatKnown04Reply.strDesc: [us] [tells] [them] [us-subj] [is] freaked out that so many people are debating this creepy meat.

PLOT_Meat_MeatKnown05Reply.strDesc: Inspecting [us]: It's a strange altar-like assembly consisting of a giant goat eye, two giant curved horns, and four oversized goat-like legs.

ENCPLOT_Meat_GoatBossStart.strDesc:
As you stare down at the strange assemblage of harvested organs, the world around you begins to quiver and bend. A dark shadow beneath the idol grows and spreads, like ink dropped in a pool of still water, until everything around you but your body and the makeshift totem is black.

The shadow recedes and you find yourself standing in the cramped central deck of a ship whose design escapes your understanding. Every surface is covered in a sinewy tangle of conduits and wiring of varying thickness, behind which a reddish glow casts faint light and long shadows. The air here is free from the sterile chemical smell of recycled oxygen. Instead it is warm and moist, like breath exhaled from a living body.

Before you, where the idol once sat, you find a long-dead Nav station. It is covered in narrow wires that run from the ground like overgrown weeds. Visible through the tangle of wires is a plate on which the ship's name is stenciled: The Lesser Key of Solomon.

Branching from the central deck you find three corridors leading to deeper cabins of specialized design. To your left there is a laboratory, to your right a crew quarters, and ahead of you, down the longest corridor, is the reactor room.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_GoLab.strDesc:
Inside the lab you find an array of rusting genetic and surgical equipment. The swollen conduits from the walls run to broken specimen tanks and now-vacant operating tables. Every surface drips with a warm, viscous liquid.

One operating table in particular catches your eye. In fact, it appears to be several tables, all of them set side by side and welded together at the center to create one overlarge surface. The arrangement sits in the center of the room, and is surrounded with crude scaffolding reaching nearly to the ceiling. Platforms are set into the scaffolding and dozens of hand lamps are clipped to it, all of them pointing down at the assembly.

Terminals line the right side of the room. One flickers to life then dies out again as a conduit beside it sparks.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Terminal.strDesc:
Rifling through the data files on the last remaining operational terminal, you discover the personal journal, trial results, and various experimental notations of one Professor Park Hyun Lee.

It's a name you recognize. Professor Lee is a notorious figure in the system, a once constant presence in the tabloid media. Formerly a renowned academic at the Korean School for Biotechnology on Kapyong Station in the Martian system, Lee's doctorate was revoked when he published a manifesto on the benefits of gene splicing between and among species.

After losing his post, Professor Lee moved on to work in various high level corporate roles, including as Chief Development Officer of Hyun Lee Petware and Chief Research Specialist at Brave New Worlds, LLC.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_GoQuarters.strDesc:
What you find here is, on first impression, a standard small crew quarters: two bunks, several storage lockers, a single sink and toilet. Personal effects lay on end tables in haphazard arrangements: eyeglasses, reading material, photographs of friends and family pinned to the walls. Four lab coats, long ago white, hang on the wall beside each bed.

As your eyes adjust to the reddish darkness, however, the scene resolves into something far more strange. The mass of conduits on every surface run towards the bunks and up into the beds. There, they disappear into a long form under  age-browned sheets, spotted with rust colored stains.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_LabSheets.strDesc:
You peel back the sodden sheets to find a sleeping malformed creature whose proportions are the only element you could reasonably describe as human.

They are nude save for the snaking conduits that run from the nest beneath them into port-like sores on their chest, arms and legs. Bristly fur covers their body in thick patches at the abdomen and upper thigh. Their jawbone is elongated and distends into a respirator of original design. Two horns poke through the matted, filthy hair at the front of their skull.

Chasing a sick sense of curiosity, you draw back the sheet further and find beneath it more hair in which nest genitals beyond your recognition. Two long, unguligrade legs bend down to a pair of cloven hooves.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_LabSheetsFail.strDesc: You are too terrified to dare peel back the sodden sheets, but you think you spot a pair of cloven hooves protruding from the bottom.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_GoReactor.strDesc:
The environment around you grows hotter and more humid with every step you take down the long corridor into the deepest bowels of the ship. As the world behind you recedes from both memory and view, the one ahead defies your understanding.

Before long, you find that a reddish musculature has begun to grow on the snaking conduits beneath you. Viscous blood pools around your feet with every soft step. Deeper in, the meat gives way for portions of skin and, deeper still, patches of bristly hair.

After what feels like more steps than the corridor demanded, you enter a darkened engineering chamber. Before you on the far wall, where the reactor should be, you instead find a massive throne of viscera, muscle, conduit, and bone.

Sitting perfectly still upon it is a human-shaped creature of monstrous scale. Though it appears to be sleeping, you can sense it is very alive. The creature is breathing in time with the ship, and all the conduits run to its throne like arteries to a beating heart.

Mingled with its more human form, the creature shows the unmistakable features of a goat: a distended snout, unguligrade legs with cloven hooves, and two huge horns on its head that suggest a casual lethality. Its meaty muscles are obscene in their size and proportion. Bristly hair gathers at its otherwise nude waist and upper thighs. The hair fails to conceal the creature's overly large phallus, the upward curve of which produces in you an unsettling mixture of emotions.

Sitting beside the throne is a scepter of spine leading to an ornamental goat's skull. From it sprouts a pair of shattered horns, forming many sharp points.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_ThroneApproach.strDesc:
You take a few halting steps towards the center of the chamber, where the reddish glow has pooled before the throne like a spotlight. Before you reach the throne, the creature's eyes flick open and find your own. The eyes are wide set, golden yellow, with a long black rectangular pupil that runs parallel to the ground.

You stand in the spotlight and meet the creature's gaze for what feels like an eternity. As you do, a terror builds in your mind like static. A wave of noise, growing in volume, through which you can distantly discern a voice breaking through. Like a transmission from far away. The voice merges and coalesces, breaks through the static, and before long, is as clear to you as if it were spoken. The words present to you in a warm, syrupy tenor, but are laced with the shiver of a panicked animal being led to slaughter.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_ThroneFlee.strDesc:
Terrified by the sight of the Goat King, you flee from the reactor room in a blind panic, your vision bleary as you run. As you tear through the corridors, the shadows again begin to grow and bend to black until, finally, they overtake your vision completely.

You jolt awake sucking air into your lungs. Before you sits the idol you were so arrogant and foolish to assemble.

The possibility you abandoned today will likely haunt you in private moments of reflection. Weeks and even years later, the Goat King will speak to you in dreams.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_ThroneCharge.strTitle: Charge in Unprepared and Strike it Down
ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_ThroneCharge.strDesc: You reach your target when The Goatman extends a hand and touches you. You feel your muscles shiver off your bones as the meat of your heart spasms.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_ThroneChargeCont.strDesc: As darkness and pain without end envelope you, all you can see, hear, and smell is Him.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Flee.strDesc: You make your way back to the shimmering distortion near the Nav station and slip through. It vanishes behind you, leaving an acrid taste in your mouth and the nagging weight of unanswered questions.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z1.strDesc:
The voice asks you who you are and why you've come. The question resonates in your mind against a deep and primal fear that gives way to rage. How dare this monstrosity question your intention? You, an enlightened and evolved creature, being challenged by an atavistic freak of science or hell. One even lower than any terrestrial beast.

And yet there remains a similarity between you and the monster. The congruity is more awful and terrifying than anything you've ever felt.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z1a.strDesc: Terrified by the voice and familiar gaze of the creature, you slink from view and seek a darkened corner of the engineering room where you crouch and wait.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z1b.strDesc: Staring at the fiend in its terrible eyes you say that you've come to challenge it, to match your own human capacity against a grotesque power that should never have entered this world in the first place.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z1c.strDesc: Before the fiend can seduce you further, you strike out at it with great prejudice, hoping to remove it from this world forever.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z1d.strDesc: Breaking free of the freakish gaze of the fiend, you dart past the being into a shadowy corner of the room in search of abandoned materials with which to build a trap. Maybe you can lure it into a position of weakness?

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z2.strDesc:
You hear a terrible bleating behind you accompanied by the clatter of hooves beating the ground. You turn just in time to see three nimble, snarling satyrs charging headlong into the room. Their eyes are bloodshot and crazed and they close upon you with impossible speed.

Just before they reach you the piercing command of the Goat King rings out in your mind, so loud that you wince in pain and are forced down to the ground. When you open your eyes the three smaller beasts staring down at you, stock still, with expressions of hatred.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z2a.strDesc: You stand to engage the vicious beasts, and launch into a tangle of sinewy limbs. Hard hooves trample upon you and sharp horns stab at your chest and neck as you strike out at anything in your sight.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z2a_Part2a.strDesc:
You have a distant impression of clutching a skull and bashing it against the wall beside you before burying your knee so deep into the belly of one beast that it instantly pukes a long string of bile and falls to the floor.

As you stand you see the final of the three minor satyrs before you clutching at its arm which is bent at an odd angle. Still staring you in the eyes, it backs into the darkened corridor, no doubt seeking a quiet place to nurse its many wounds.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z2a_Part2b.strDesc: The rain of blows from the satyrs is too much, however. Cracks of bone sound in your skull, hooves shove through your flesh, and bursts of warm liquid spill through your body as it crumples limply to the floor.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z2b.strDesc:
You stand and stare down the three beasts before you. On closer inspection, you see remnants of their former humanity: tattered clothes, the soft curve of an earlobe, four fingers on each hand beside a dirty thumb.

You ask them who they were before and why they are here. They stare back at you with impressions impossible to discern. You tell them who you are, where you've come from.

You see no change in their expressions. But one of the creatures tilts its head at an odd angle as you speak. Soon, it turns around and walks down the long corridor, no doubt returning to the crew quarters to rest.

Enough. The word enters your mind in the Goat King's voice, and you turn to face him.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z2c.strDesc:
You stand and turn to face the Goat King. Even sitting on the throne he towers above you, and you have to tilt your face to meet his terrible gaze. Imagining how you'll lunge at him through the satyrs, you tense.

But at the first sign of your movement, the satyrs pounce. They were ready, and reading you for any sign of hostility.

Three beasts in prime physical condition pummel your body with hardened fists and hooves. Covering your body with every limb you can free, you try to withstand the blows, and look for any opportunity to counter.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z2d.strDesc:
Learning you are not alone with the King changes the equation. If you had ever hoped to slay this horrible beast, that hope has curdled into a desperate need to escape this place with your life intact.

You make your way back to the shimmering distortion near the Nav station and slip through. It vanishes behind you, leaving an acrid taste in your mouth and the nagging weight of unanswered questions.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z3.strDesc: As the fiend sits before you, you know in your heart what must be done.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z3a.strDesc:
Steeling yourself against the fear, you remind yourself that you brought a weapon into the portal for this very purpose. As you retrieve it, the Goat King stands from his throne and picks up the spinal scepter beside him.

The swing comes immediately, and you almost don't have time to react. The Goat King's scepter smashes into the meaty ground, sending a huge splash of thickened blood up from where you were just a moment ago. As the blow rebounds, the entire ship contracts around it, and the Goat King himself staggers, clutching at his own stomach.

Seeing your opening, you strike out with your weapon and deliver a wound to the Goat King's side, just below its exposed ribs. The King swings out again, this time connecting with your legs, which disappear from under you and you fall to the ground.

Another blow falls, and again you manage to escape it, this time rolling away as the scepter smashes down beside you. A cracking, like bone, is heard from deep within the hull of the ship. The Goat King cries out again, this time stumbling and clutching its own leg.

You stand and swing at the injured leg, a blow that sends the Goat King kneeling as if waiting to be knighted. With your last ounce of strength you bring your weapon down upon its filthy head. It splits open and the King collapses.

The ship continues to sputter and groan around you. Knowing your work here is done, pry the spinal scepter from the King's grasp, and return to the shimmering portal at the Nav station in the center of the ship. You step through it and return to the world you left behind. In your hand you find the scepter, the only evidence you'll ever have of the horrible encounter.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z3b.strDesc:
Steeling yourself against the fear, you remember that you have a tool on your person that might serve well in this instance. As you retrieve it, the Goat King stands from his throne and picks up the spinal scepter beside him.

The swing comes immediately, and you almost don't have time to react. The Goat King's scepter smashes into the meaty ground, sending a huge splash of thickened blood up from where you were just a moment ago. As the blow rebounds, the entire ship contracts around it, and the Goat King himself staggers, clutching at his own stomach.

Seeing your opening, you strike out with your improvised weapon and deliver a wound to the Goat King's side, just below its exposed ribs. The King swings out again, this time connecting with your legs, which disappear from under you and you fall to the ground.

Another blow falls and again you manage to escape it, this time rolling away as the scepter smashes down beside you. The huge blow cracks a bone deep within the hull of the ship. The Goat King cries out again and stumbles back clutching its own leg.

You stand and swing at the injured leg, a blow that sends the Goat King kneeling before you like a night awaiting the touch of the sword upon his shoulders. With your last ounce of strength you bring your tool down upon its filthy head. The King's skull splits open and his body collapses.

The ship continues to sputter and groan around you. Knowing your work here is done, pry the spinal scepter from the King's grasp, and return to the shimmering portal at the Nav station in the center of the ship. You step through it and return to the world you left behind. In your hand you find the scepter, the only evidence you'll ever have of the horrible encounter.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z3c.strDesc:
Steeling yourself against the fear, you remember that you've trained your body and fought enough to rise to this occasion. You move your feet into a stable brawling stance and watch as the Goat King stands from his throne and picks up the spinal scepter beside him.

The swing comes so fast that your body dodges it before your mind has a chance to react. The Goat King's scepter smashes into the meaty ground in a huge splash of thickened blood. As the blow falls, the entire ship contracts around it, and the Goat King himself staggers, clutching at his own stomach.

Seeing your opening, you kick at the Goat King's side, striking it just below its exposed ribs. The King swings out again, this time connecting with your legs, which disappear from under you and you fall to the ground.

Another blow falls and again you manage to escape it, this time rolling away as the scepter smashes down beside you. The huge blow cracks a bone deep within the hull of the ship. The Goat King cries out again and stumbles back clutching its own leg.

You stand and swing at the injured leg, a blow that sends the Goat King kneeling before you like a knight awaiting the touch of the sword upon his shoulders. With your last ounce of strength you bring your hands together into a fist and bring it down on the creature's head. The King's skull splits open and his body collapses.

The ship continues to sputter and groan around you. Knowing your work here is done, pry the spinal scepter from the King's grasp, and return to the shimmering portal at the Nav station in the center of the ship. You step through it and return to the world you left behind. In your hand you find the scepter, the only evidence you'll ever have of the horrible encounter.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_Z3d.strDesc:
Steeling yourself against the fear, you remind yourself that you brought a firearm into the portal for this very purpose. As you retrieve it, the Goat King stands from his throne and picks up the spinal scepter beside him.

The swing comes immediately, and you almost don't have time to react. The Goat King's scepter smashes into the meaty ground, sending a huge splash of thickened blood up from where you were just a moment ago. As the blow rebounds, the entire ship contracts around it, and the Goat King himself staggers, clutching at his own stomach.

Seeing your opening, you level your weapon and fire into the Goat King's side, just below its exposed ribs. The King stumbles but then swings out again, this time connecting with your legs, which disappear from under you. You fall to the ground and your gun tumbles away into the darkness.

Another blow falls and again you manage to escape it, this time rolling away as the scepter smashes down beside you. The huge blow cracks a bone deep within the hull of the ship. The Goat King cries out again and stumbles back clutching its own leg.

You roll further into the darkness and find your weapon. You stand, level it, and fire at the injured leg. The shot sends the Goat King kneeling down as if waiting to be knighted. With your last ounce of strength you aim at the creature's skull and squeeze the trigger. The King's head explodes in a rain of gore and its body collapses to the ground.

The ship continues to sputter and groan around you. Knowing your work here is done, pry the spinal scepter from the King's grasp, and return to the shimmering portal at the Nav station in the center of the ship. You step through it and return to the world you left behind. In your hand you find the scepter, the only evidence you'll ever have of the horrible encounter.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M1.strDesc:
Standing before the creature, you know what you're seeing is impossible by every metric. Biology, Physics, Anatomy: the vision lives in defiance of all the knowledge systems you've trusted for your entire life.

And yet, here it sits. The impossible. While there have been rumors of rare and unique animals as long as there has been civilization, few have come face to face with something as horrific and strange as what appears before you now.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M1a.strDesc:
In some ways, you are lucky to be here. Surely you're the first of mankind to see such a creature. You give yourself time to admire the specimen: the long snout, the rectangular pupils, the impossibly musculature of its hulking body.

The strangest feature by far, however, are the hulking unguligrade legs. You've never seen such a backwards bend on a bi-pedal creature in all your life.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M1b.strDesc:
No. This simply cannot be. The only explanation is that you're in a dream.

Remembering an old superstition, you grab at the flesh of your arm and pinch the skin, hard enough to make you wince.

When you open your watering eyes the creature still sits before you, stone still, awaiting some reply.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M1c.strDesc:
At the end of the day, meat is meat. It's something you've seen before, though admittedly in somewhat less anthropomorphic forms.

You retrieve the tools of your trade and prepare to break down the form for resources: skin from meat, meat from bone, organs from within, some more useful than others.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M1d.strDesc:
You know that even in impossible situations, safety only comes to those who prepare for catastrophe. Regardless of how the creature before you pushes the boundaries of your sanity, you steel your mind against it.

You preempt disaster by imagining it in narrative detail: your maiming, your death, the wholesale destruction of the entire system; none if it is surprising when it is rehearsed and lived in your imagination enough.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M2.strDesc:
Before you can continue, the creature's voice breaks through the noise in your mind and speaks to you with surprising clarity. The voice is sonorous and warbling, and it makes a compelling case that mankind has always been an evolving species.

What began as a singular drive for a fish to pull itself out of warm waters of the sea has become, against all odds, a brilliant culture scattered across the entire solar system. What's more, each and every member within this culture holds fast to that self same drive to push further, to push for more, even if it means certain death.

Why, then, should we fear the next stage in our evolution? Why run from the chance to be faster, to be stronger, to be more resilient against the harsh realities of the cold, airless, and uncaring atmosphere in which humanity now finds itself?

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M2a.strDesc:
Drawn by the rationality of the case, you offer your own rebuttal. It addresses the creature's argument in all the particulars, and its totality rebuts the opposing case in the general. Your position pushes beyond the original and even surfaces edge cases the creature may not have considered.

It is a good argument and you're proud of it.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M2b.strDesc: You close your eyes and remind yourself once again that this is not happening. It is not happening because it cannot happen. Men do not become goats. If they did, they would not have the power to speak telepathically. Ships cannot live. If they did, they would not bleed, they would not breathe.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M2c.strDesc:
You consider the argument. Frankly, the case is well made. It's hard to refute from a utilitarian perspective. And yet, like all utilitarian arguments, what it lacks is humanity. Of course on a grand scale the argument holds true. But what of the humans in the here, in the now? Are they to be made to suffer so that the species can expand? 

You explain this, as well as you can to a freakish bi-pedal half man half goat. The creature appears to listen, but you can't be too sure.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M2d.strDesc:
It's true. Every word. Why limit the power of the species? What good is delaying change when change is inevitable?

Awed to silence by the creature's logic, you kneel before him and submit yourself to its power. You volunteer your body to be the first among those chosen. You beg. Plead.

Your new King stands and stares down at you. From the depths in the noise in your mind you hear a faint chuckle that grows into a snicker before becoming, finally a hideous choking laugh.

And what, the King asks, makes you think you are worthy, hm? Because you found me? Here? And what? You believe yourself to be the first.

No, no no. You are not the first. Nor, I'm afraid, will you be the last.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M3.strDesc:
You've indulged the creature for long enough. Why continue to chase insanity when a perfectly rational path lays before you?

You take a deep breath, step forward, and prepare to subdue the creature. As you do, it seems to shrink in size before your eyes. By the time you reach the throne and grasp it, you find it's far smaller even than you.

The tiny, bleating freak of nature puts up a worthy fight but in the end you manage to render it unconscious, hog tie it, and drag it down the corridor to the lab.

Now to decide what to do with the thing.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M3a.strTitle: Keep Clean and Harvest What you Can
ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M3a.strDesc:
You start by scrubbing the lab down and creating a somewhat sanity working environment. Knowing your work here will be longer than just a day, you go to the crew quarters and do the same.

You gather tools, lay out the specimen on an operating table, and set to work.

After a few long days of research and experimentation you've managed to extract the cuts of meat that show signs of hyper metastasizing. You lay these into a scratch-built incubator and hope for the best.

Your work pays off in just a few more days. Just as you hypothesized, the assembly produces what appears to be safe and edible protein at an extremely rapid rate.

With your work here done, you bring the assembly to the portal near the Nav station at the center of the ship and return to where you came from, invention in hand.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M3b.strDesc:
Grabbing some cutting instruments from a locker in the lab you set about butchering the creature. In some respects it is not so different from working with any other animal. But when you are forced to remove the hands, your stomach does turn a bit.

You set aside a few cuts of meat for further study, and set to cooking and eating the rest. It doesn't taste so bad, all things considered. A bit gamey, perhaps, but far nicer than standard spacer fare.

You spend the next few days researching the extracted cuts of meat and find that they show signs of hyper metastasizing. You lay these into a scratch built incubator and hope for the best.

Your work pays off in just a few more days. Just as you hypothesized, the assembly produces what appears to be safe and edible protein at an extremely rapid rate.

With your work here done, you bring the assembly to the portal near the Nav station at the center of the ship and return to where you came from, invention in hand.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_M3c.strDesc:
You retrieve a cutting instrument from a locker in the lab and set to removing the creature's heart. It's grisly work, but after cracking open the sternum you find a bi-valve human heart with cardiological features suggesting exceptional efficiency. You remove it, along with a few cuts of muscle, and reserve them for further study.

After a few long days of research and experimentation on the heart you find first that you can reverse engineer a subcutaneous treatment paired with consuming parts of the heart to permanently improve your own cariovascular efficiency. Secondly, you find that the tissue shows signs of hyper metastasizing. You lay portions into a scratch-built incubator and hope for the best.

Your work pays off in just a few more days. Just as you hypothesized, the assembly produces what appears to be safe and edible protein at an extremely rapid rate.

With your work here done, you bring the assembly to the portal near the Nav station at the center of the ship and return to where you came from, invention in hand.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C1.strDesc:
Seated before you is the object of your seeking. A creature whose power is beyond any human imagination. A being whose name is heard only in darkened corners of the system, and even then, told only in whispers: The Goat Without End.

In his yellowed eyes you see knowledge of all the veiled mysteries in the universe. But how will you attain it?

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C1a.strDesc:
The terror of the moment falls upon you like a sudden illness. The fever begins in your shoulders and creeps down the middle of your back and comes to rest at the bottom of your spine.

Your body folds involuntarily: first at the knees, then at the waist, and finally at the neck. You press your forehead into the bloody sinew of the floor and hope, desperately, that the deity before you chooses not to strike you dead.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C1b.strDesc: You shower the deity with eloquent praise, some of which is genuine. You offer worship to his power, his poise, the clarity of his vision. You regale the King with rumors of his strength passed throughout the system.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C1c.strDesc: You recall seeing a rusting workblade near the entrance of the chamber. You retrieve it, and in full view of The Goat Without End, you draw a long cut across your palm. A stinging pain gives way to an awful dull ache as hot blood runs down the length of your arm.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C1d.strDesc: You kneel before The Goat Without End and ask for its discerning eyes upon you. Prostrating yourself against the living floor you beg to gain access to the knowledge that lies behind the veil of this paltry reality.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C2.strDesc:
In the distance you hear an awful wailing. Slowly, the king raises its arm and extends a long finger towards the corridor behind you. You turn to face the sound and find, emerging from the gloom, two small and hideous satyrs holding between them a filthy shackled human with a bag over their head.

The creatures drag the prisoner towards the throne and toss them onto the ground between you and The King. Distracted as you are by the pitiful moans emanating from beneath the hood, it takes you a moment to see the ornate dagger lying on the ground before you.

You look up into the yellow, wide set eyes of The Goat Without End, and know beyond any doubt what the deity is asking of you.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C2a.strDesc:
You grab the dagger and stab at the human form indiscriminately. It screams and writhes, trying desperately to roll away, but you continue the task with a crazed persistence.

You're shocked by how exhausted you are when the grisly work is through. Sweat drips down your face. Your forearms are covered in dark blood.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C2b.strDesc:
You can't. You won't. No matter how much you crave the knowledge that the King Without End can give, what the deity is asking for now is simply too much.

You stand and say nothing. After a long and awful silence, the satyrs retrieve the hooded prisoner and drag them back down the corridor.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C2c.strDesc:
This isn't what you signed up for and you'd rather not be involved. You tell this to the deity and his minions and hope for the best.

You stand patiently, awaiting a reply. After a long and awful silence, the satyrs retrieve the hooded prisoner and drag them back down the corridor.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C2d.strDesc:
Looking down at the dagger and the wretched hooded figure before you, you can't help but feel a little embarrassed. Where is the altar? The ancient manuscript? The golden chalice in which to collect the sacrificial blood?

You point this out to the King, as well as a few other haphazard details, and suggest, politely, that you expected more from a being of such greatness and renown.

The goatman stares down at you, expressionless.

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C3.strDesc:
The voice of The King breaks through the static in your mind and calls you by your name.

A vessel, it says in its warbling double voice. One who can receive The Gift.

Is it you? How can I be sure?

ENCPlot_Meat_GoatBoss_C3a.strDesc:
You prostrate yourself before your King and beg for The Gift. You grovel so deeply that you feel like you might sink into the floor.

The deity beckons you closer and you step towards the throne.You bow before him and the Goat Without End extends a huge hand that he places upon your head.

In an instant your mind is flooded with images you've never seen and thoughts you've never had. Possibility stretches before you as plains towards an infinitely receding horizon. For a brief moment you possess a knowledge so complete and wonderful it is as if you have become one with the universe itself.

And then the pain arrives. An itching and then burning in your eyes that is so intense you cannot manage a single thought. You feel your eyeballs expand, your irises distend, and your pupils flatten before passing out from the pain.

You jolt awake sucking air into your lungs. Before you sits the idol you were so arrogant and foolish to assemble. Finally outside the living ship, you breathe the familiar atmosphere of recycled oxygen but it does nothing to dispel your deep sense of dread.

Slowly you bring your hand to your face. You touch your mouth, your cheeks, and, cautiously, your eyes, to find what you already know to be true. The eyes of The Goat. It's a curse that will stay with you until the day that you die.

PLOT_Merga_WhispersFound01.strTooltip: Pay more attention to the news to learn details about a beloved entertainer missing from Venus.
PLOT_Merga_WhispersFound01.strDesc:
A knot of curious spacers gather around the television and murmur to one another as the OWNG "News in Brief" program updates the Inner Planets on the latest goings on. 

You cram yourself between two distraught union workers in EVA suits to catch a glimpse of what is causing such a stir. On screen you see footage of a beautiful woman in a red dress. The montage moves through sequences in rapid pace: the woman on stage singing in a moody lounge ahead of velvet drapes, the same woman fleeing paparazzi photographers and pulling her sunglasses down over her eyes, a sequence of photographs of her arm-in-arm with a dashing athlete you don't recognize. 

Superimposed above all of this is an alarming chyron scrolling in bold letters: 

VENUSIAN POP ICON CAMILLIA MIDDLEMIST, AKA MISS M, STILL MISSING.

Beside you a young woman lowers her head and brings her hand to her eyes.

"That arrogant fucker," she mutters to nobody in particular.

"Who?" you ask.

"Who do you think," she says, and nods towards the screen. The footage shows the dashing athlete again, Rex Korin, this time stepping into a nimble RCS racer at the Encantado Grand Prix. Later footage shows Korin hoisting the trophy.

"Those hotshit nitro-burners are all the same," the woman says, and then walks away to gather herself. 

A sidebar shows a schedule for the upcoming broadcast. Most of the spacers gathered seem glued to the TV.

PLOT_Merga_WhispersFound01Reply.strTitle: Newsroom with Trevor Bank: Who Was Miss M?
PLOT_Merga_WhispersFound01Reply.strDesc:
The program begins as it always does: a brief animation of the title that zooms in on the host's name before it races off through a render of the Inner System, passing above all the planets until eventually landing on Mars and falling into an austere studio where Banks sits beside his cohost, Weihan Wing. 

Banks, usually a model of stoicism and state-enforced Martian "objectivity," seems tired and sad. The host reports that the hour will be dedicated to a history of the missing Miss M. The proceedings carry a distinct elegiac tone. 

Before this, Banks restates the obvious: Camellia Middlemist, famed Venusian pop icon beloved system wide, has been missing for nearly four days. The authorities have brought in Rex Korin, her recent spouse, for questioning. No leads have been made in the case. 

The host throws to Weihan, who offers a survey of Middlemist's rich biography.

ENCPLOT_Merga_SuperfanBossStart.strDesc:
You find the superfan and grill them about the footage you found. It's a strange interrogation at first. Every question and demand is met with a giggle or coy smile, no matter how serious the matter at hand.

Maybe sensing an angle, your detective partner lays on the bad cop act, lacing their tone with parental admonishments and scolding. The dam breaks. In an instant the superfan's eerie smile melts into an expression of childish rage and confusion.

"He promised," the superfan manages through bitter tears. "He promised to make her love me."

"Who promised?"

"The cloaked one. With hollow eyes."

"I need you to tell me exactly what he said."

"He said if I told him where Miss M was that night that he would give her the gifts I bought her. That she wouldn't refuse them anymore. That she would take me instead of that awful cop she was always with."

"What cop," the detective asks.

"You know what cop," the superfan replies. "Your little friend. Tanner."

"And if he couldn't? Couldn't convince her?"

 "He promised," the superfan tries. "That he would make her pay. For choosing Tanner instead of me. Oh god I'm so sorry..."

The superfan breaks into racking sobs and continues pleading the detective and Miss M for forgiveness for what they've done.

ENCPlot_Merga_Superfan_Arrest.strDesc:
You cuff the sniveling superfan and take them in for processing.

You lead with the suspect's access to the victim and failed alibi and leave out their crazed tale of the cloaked accomplice. It's more than enough to convince the upper LEO brass and with the entire system begging for a head to roll in the case, you're certain the NewCal DA will convict without much difficulty.

News of your work on the case circulates quickly among the ranks of the Venusian police. After a meeting with a handful of the department upper brass, you're assured that if you ever find yourself in trouble with the law in and around Venus, it will turn out to be no trouble at all. 

When the dust settles the detective thanks you for your help and offers their assistance if you ever need it in the future.

"One more thing," they say before you leave. "What our suspect said about the cloaked figure reminds me of something Josephus Tanner told me about when he was at his worst. Come with me. We should tie up one last loose end."

ENCPlot_Merga_Superfan_Kill.strDesc:
Together you lead the blubbering superfan through non trafficked maintenance corridors towards the LA Aerostat, ignoring their pleas all the way. As you do so you're met with the uncanny feeling that this is something your detective friend has done before. 

You reach an abandoned garbage airlock and stuff the superfan inside. There's a brief moment when you wonder who will open the trap door on the other side. You suddenly realize it doesn't matter. You press the button to open the floor and the sniveling accomplice to murder falls to their certain death through Venus's sulfurous, caustic fog.

The detective turns to you with a look in their eyes you've never seen before.

"You're mine now," they say. "Forever. Whatever I ask of you. No questions. When I say jump, you say how high. And if you ever speak of this to anyone, you'll find yourself begging for the mercy we just showed that scumbag. 

Lastly, you'll need this. For when shit hits the fan."

The detective hands you a briefcase. You're surprised by how heavy it is and wonder what could be inside.

"First order of business: what our suspect said about the cloaked figure reminds me of something Josephus Tanner told me about when he was at his worst. Come with me."

ENCPLOT_Merga_RacerBossStart.strDesc:
You find the racing icon sipping Cachaca and lime in a dark corner of the Sol Vermelho Lounge. He raises the glass to you as you approach. 

"Rare Earth vintage," he says. "Might be the last bottle in the System."

"Lime ain't cheap, either," the detective mutters. 

"So?" the racer asks. "This better be quick. I have a shuttle headed to Hangzhou in an hour."

You tell him about the false alibi, how nobody could fly like that while drunk, even them.

"Proves nothing," the racer says before taking a sip. "She died with a handprint like the rest of them."

"Faked," the detective says. "Checked the body an hour ago. Whatever you used to stain it on matches what we found all over your favorite seat here in the bar. I'm sure we'll find traces of it in your ship when we seize it tonight."

The racing icon stares at you for a long moment, drains his drink, then looks up at the stage.

"This is where we fell in love, you know" they say. "She was singing Mas Que Nada."

"Why, then?" you ask. "Why kill her?"

The racer wheels towards the detective, tears of rage welling in his eyes. 

"Why don't you ask your partner, you son of a bitch?"

"Tanner?"

"Pigs," the racer scoffs. "You're all the same. Think everything in the world belongs to you."

The racing icon wipes his eyes and takes a long look at the detective. "But I have a feeling Tanner isn't going to be much of a problem to anyone anymore.

ENCPlot_Merga_Racer_Arrest.strDesc:
You cuff Korin and take him in for processing. Sure enough, a material analysis of his champion racing vessel yields trace amounts of the same compound stained on Middlemist's hip. It's not a job he could have done alone, but even without accomplices, the evidence is enough to put the champion racer away for a long time.

News of your work on the case circulates quickly among the ranks of the Venusian police. After a meeting with a handful of the department upper brass, you're assured that if you ever find yourself in trouble with the law in and around Venus, it will turn out to be no trouble at all.

When the dust settles the detective thanks you for your help and offers their assistance if you ever need it in the future.

 "One more thing," they say before you leave. "What Korin said about Tanner still isn't sitting right. Come with me. We should tie up one last loose end."

ENCPlot_Merga_Racer_Kill.strDesc:
The detective cuffs a defiant Rex Korin, and together, you lead him through non-trafficked maintenance corridors towards the LA Aerostat. Ignoring his insults on the way, you're faced with the uncanny feeling that this is something the detective has done before.

You reach an abandoned garbage airlock, and it's only then Rex drops his tough guy act. Against his pleas, you stuff him inside. There's a brief moment when you wonder who will open the trap door on the other side. You suddenly realize it doesn't matter. You press the button to open the floor, and the arrogant accomplice to murder disappears through Venus's sulfurous, caustic fog.

The detective turns to you with a look in their eyes you've never seen before.

"You're mine now," they say. "Forever. Whatever I ask of you. No questions. When I say jump, you say how high. And if you ever speak of this to anyone, you'll find yourself begging for the mercy we just showed that scumbag."

 Lastly, you'll need this. For when shit hits the fan."

The detective hands you a briefcase. You're surprised by how heavy it is and wonder what could possibly be inside.

"First order of business: what was said about the cloaked figure reminds me of something Josephus Tanner told me about when he was at his worst. Come with me."

ENCPlot_Merga_Boss_GoXXX1.strDesc:
The detective is silent as you follow them down increasingly shabby corridors deep in the Encantado favelas. Far from the bright and airy world of the aerostat in the upper levels, the world you find yourself in now is dim, the air fouled by the aroma of industries most Venusians pretend don't exist: the acrid tang of formaldehyde in the morgue, earthy notes from food processing plants, all of it laced with sickly sulfurous tones emanating from nearby waste processing facilities. 

The journey terminates in front of a huge red door in what appears to be a warehouse repurposed for illegal housing. The detective approaches the keypad and pauses.

"I wish I could tell you what we're in for, but the truth is I have no idea," they say."Tanner started in the deep end with the handprint murders, and only fell deeper after getting involved with Miss M. He kept saying there was a danger he could never share. Brace yourself."

ENCPlot_Merga_Boss_GoXXX2.strDesc:
You enter the space and learn that if Josephus Tanner was once a respected law enforcement officer his home makes it clear he's since fallen far from grace. The walls are invisible behind stacks of boxes overflowing with papers and data files. The ground is littered with discarded take out cartons. A shabby sleeping sack is bundled in one corner.

The filth is ringed around three huge boards festooned with photographs and paraphernalia connected by a crazed web of red string. Before the board stands a hunched black form leaking shadows from its edges. The air around it dances with tongues of black flame. You watch as the form plucks a photograph like a ripe fruit, examines it, then sets it ablaze with a dark and smokeless fire.

ENCPlot_Merga_Boss_GoXXX3.strDesc:
"Police! Hands behind your head," shouts the detective before drawing their weapon. In an instant the form blinks a hundred and eighty degrees and freezes as still as a photograph. A pale face sits atop the creature and stares through you with enormous hollow eyes. Your entire body goes cold and you are unable to move. Your vision blurs and in a second instant the form is gone, leaving behind it nothing but the distinct odor of burned carbon. 

On closer inspection the board reveals a nearly incomprehensible conspiracy stretching across the entire system over decades. Just when the story seems to coalesce there are pieces missing, some leaving behind charred remains. The longer you stare at the story the less sense it seems to make. Two names stand out, however: Ursula and Philip.

When you finally tear yourself away from the board you see the detective standing in a dark corner above a filthy cot surrounded by jars of various fluids. The body on the makeshift bed is in the fetal position, turned away from you, its pale lower back exposed.

A black bruise stares up at you from Josephus Tanner's long dead body. It is in the shape of a long fingered hand.

The detective turns to you with a grim expression, their eyes welling up with tears.

"I have no idea what Tanner was looking into here. But it was dangerous. And that...thing we just saw? I never want to see anything like it again. I don't know how you feel about it but I suggest we bury this. All of it. It's the only way I'd feel safe."

ENCPlot_Merga_Boss_BuryEnding.strDesc:
You scrub the warehouse of all traces of Tanner's work. The detective places their former partner's body on a dolly and carts it to a nearby industrial district. With that grim work out of mind, you dismantle Tanner's evidence board without another thought of what story it might tell. You pile it on a second dolly and meet the detective at an incinerator.

Together you shovel Tanner's obsession onto the blazing pyre where it disappears alongside his body. You shake the detective's hand and part ways, knowing that you'll never speak of this to them, or anyone, ever again.

Your life moves forward accompanied by a strange sense that you're being watched. No matter what you do, you can't shake the feeling that one day the story you destroyed will catch up with you. That you'll be asked to return to it, and that you won't have the bravery to refuse.

ENCPlot_Merga_Boss_PublicEnding.strDesc:
Ignoring the detective's pleas you dismantle Tanner's conspiracy board and pile the remaining documents into boxes. You collate them as best you can, but the truth is that it is impossible to make sense of sprawling narrative, especially with vital pieces missing or partially burned. But you know someone who can. 

The journalist is surprised to see you given that they were a prime suspect in M's murder. But even if you can't fully trust them, you both understand nobody else in the system has the skills and knowledge to understand the story Tanner was trying to tell. You leave the boxes with them, along with all your hope that anyone will ever know why Middlemist died the way she did.

Over the next few days the journalist releases a slow trickle of news about what are now dubbed The Tanner Files. Based on what you read in those articles, you know it will take months, even years before anything has the chance of making sense.

Soon after you receive another strange message from Ursula. She thanks you for your work on the case, and tells you that you now play a part in something bigger than yourself. The message ends with a cryptic note that you'll be hearing from her again.

ENCPlot_Merga_Boss_CFinal.strDesc:
For now, though, there is little to do but wait until that day arrives.

Time to get back to work.

SHIPRumorNothing.strDesc: Whole lotta nothing, [them-regID]. I'm beginning to think we're the only two ships out here.

SHIPRumorSpam.strDesc: Another ship got spammed an empty packet. Uncompressed, all zeroes. Fifth time this week. Either someone is playing a prank or...well, I don't know what.

SHIPRumorFreezer.strDesc: A couple of dopes in the OE managed to get themselves locked in the Mescaform freezer. Barkeep found them the next morning frostbitten and drunk as all sin. One of them lost a finger.

SHIPRumorFightClub.strDesc: There's a fight club on OKLG, apparently. Bunch of desk jockeys getting their anger out. Not a fighter myself, but I'd take a gander.

SHIPRumorUnion.strDesc: Breaker's Union can't get enough support from the rank and file for a strike. I'm starting to think Ayo is seeding it with saboteurs.

SHIPRumorMariner1.strDesc: Folks keep saying they're seeing something purple floating outside their ship. Ever heard of The Mariner? I'm not superstitious myself but that one...that one gets me.

SHIPRumorMariner2.strDesc: More and more punk kids wearing purple and getting stoned on OKLG. I know what they're getting at, who they are trying to meet. But I'm not gonna say it.

SHIPRumorVenusPiracy.strDesc: Piracy is completely out of control around the Venus aerostats. They hit a dozen ships last week. Folks won't even fly from Newcal to Encantado to watch the races. Shameful shit if you ask me.

SHIPRumorPAClerk1.strDesc: New clerk at the Port Authority seems like a pushover. Buddy of mine sweet talked her way out of a few docking fees. She's a looker, but still.

SHIPRumorPAClerk2.strDesc: New clerk at the Port Authority scares easy. They dropped my docking fee after I gave them the ol' prison yard stare. Who says you can't learn anything in the joint?

SHIPRumorStatic.strDesc: Buddy of mine, a porter, heard something banging around one of their empty cabins the other night. Thought it was a stowaway. When they checked the cams, though, there was static in the center of the picture, near the bed. Damndest thing.

SHIPRumorLesserKey.strDesc: You remember that ship that escaped the Perpetual Protein lab breach? Name of The Lesser Key of Solomon? I heard it was spotted along the Ganymed orbit.

SHIPRumorVatCat.strDesc: I've been seeing more and more of those vat grown cats, you know? From Hyun Lee Petware? I don't understand the appeal myself.

SHIPRumorProtein.strDesc: I don't understand why everyone is so freaked out about the Perpetual Protein thing. Meat is meat, as far as I'm concerned. You think Trencher's is any better?

SHIPRumorLee.strDesc: That Professor Park Hyun Lee is a true bastard. Unleashing that monstrosity on the world. And for what? G-mod goat meat? Space him, I say.

SHIPRumorGoatShanty.strDesc: Two horns, two eyes and a smiling tooth. Arranged just above his cloven hoof. Then from the void you'll hear the drums. For this is how the Goatman comes.

SHIPRumorProkofiev.strDesc: Heard some freak managed to climb up the well at Prokofiev, if you can believe it.

SHIPRumorLuscaFood.strDesc: You ever tried lusca before? A buddy of mine says they serve it at weddings on Hangzhou. Melts like butter, he said.

SHIPRumorOssifex.strDesc: I've been off of long-hauling for so long now, my body aches when I put my boots on. I gotta get a line on some Ossifex.

SHIPRumorLEO1.strDesc: The Harbourmaster has been more paranoid than usual lately. Has a private detail guarding his quarters all night. Running 12 hour shifts. The whole thing has become a huge drain on department resources.

SHIPRumorLEO2.strDesc: We keep seeing tags of the number 79 around the station, especially over there in the OE? I think it's bored kids but my boss insists it's some kind of cult.

SHIPRumorLEO3.strDesc: I don't know what to make of this living meat story. Everyone I've seen talk about it seems half-insane.

SHIPJustAPrank.strTitle: Just a prank, relax and besides this is only MS13, you cannot shoot me :-P

ENCHeatEJDRFineFinish.strDesc:
After processing, you are unceremoniously dumped outside the Jade Rabbit Security Office. If you weren't docked at station when you were arrested, you may need to use the PASS ferry service (on your PDA) to reach your ship again. Hopefully it's still there.

ENCHeatEJDRPrisonStart.strDesc: You are hauled off to Jade Rabbit Brig.

ENCHeatEJDRPrisonEnd.strDesc:
You spend months laboring without wage among outcasts both meek and dangerous. You share a dorm with nearly a hundred other souls, all of you stacked like kindling on triple high bunks.

But even a hell like this is not without opportunity. You hear things. You meet people. You get in a few scrapes, you find a few friends. By the end of your term you've lived a dozen lives and you have all the scars to prove it.

Plus, free room and board. In a certain light, it might all be worth it ...

At the hearing, you can beg for just a fine- $15,000 payable in full or installments- or it's off to Tharsis Landing Brig for a year or three of hard labor.

ENCHeatMHNGFineEnd.strDesc:
It's almost like they want you to break the rules so they can extract more fines from you.

You sign reams of paperwork in tight cuffs.

It's a prison sentence of another sort. Another weight hanging around your neck.

New $15,000 fine added.

ENCHeatMHNGFineDebtEnd.strTitle: Plead for a fine (Paid in installments)
ENCHeatMHNGFineDebtEnd.strDesc:
It's almost like they want you to break the rules so they can lock you deeper in interest payments.

You sign reams of paperwork in tight cuffs.

It's a prison sentence of another sort. Another weight hanging around your neck.

New $15,000 debt added, with payment due each shift.

ENCHeatMHNGFineFinish.strDesc:
After processing, you are unceremoniously dumped outside the Tharsis Security Office. If you weren't docked at station when you were arrested, you may need to use the PASS ferry service (on your PDA) to reach your ship again. Hopefully it's still there.

Time to get back on your feet.

ENCEmbassyServicesBCER.strTitle: Select Desired Services (GalCon: Ceres and Ganymede)
ENCEmbassyServicesBCER.strDesc:
Most sovereignties in the System observe a tiered immigration status, or "strata." Usually ranging from undocumented (illegal) immigrant, up to full citizenship, a person's strata dictates which rights they enjoy with the sovereignty.

Rights can include access to certain areas or services, eligibility for private housing or ship docking, enhanced prices on trade authorization, or even legal protections or permissions.

Such rights are usually conferred by parents through birth (jus sanguinis), and in some cases, by being born in the territory (jus soli).

Obtaining legal status after birth usually involves applying for a visa, and may include getting a sponsor and/or paying a significant fee.

ENCEmbassyServicesBCERVisaInvestor.strDesc:
Cost: $5,000,000

Galilean Confederacy's Platinum Candidate (PC) targets immigrant entrepreneurs with the skills and potential to build businesses in Port Mojave that are innovative, can create jobs within the Galilean Confederacy, and can compete on a System-wide scale.

Do you have an innovative business idea, and the means to grow your business? If you can prove your ability to contribute to the advancement of Galilean Confederacy, you may be able to immigrate with this visa class.

ENCEmbassyServicesBCERVisaInvestorAccept.strDesc:
After submitting your application fee, your information is vetted through a cursory background check. Galilean Confederacy Immigration & Naturalization Authority (INA) could still discover a problem with your application during its full investigation, but at least the preliminary check passes.

Congratulations! You are now the proud holder of Permanent Resident status in the Galilean Confederacy!

Go enjoy the trade discounts and private housing opportunities.

ENCEmbassyServicesBCERVisaSkilledLabor.strDesc:
Cost: $750,000

The Skilled Laborer (SL) program is one of Galilean Confederacy's Platinum Development Board (PDB) systems for processing immigration applications. The SL program allows candidates with foreign work experience and no connections to Galilean Confederacy to apply for permanent residency.

In order to qualify for SL, a candidate must have work experience in one of the following in-demand skills:

-Excavation
-Civil Engineering
-Electrical Engineering

Those meeting the skill requirements with sufficient funds have an option to purchase this status.

ENCEmbassyServicesBCERVisaSkilledLaborAc.strTitle: Pay for Skilled Labor GalCon visa
ENCEmbassyServicesBCERVisaSkilledLaborAc.strDesc:
After submitting your application fee, your information is vetted through a cursory background check. Galilean Confederacy Immigration & Naturalization Authority (INA) assesses your proficiency in the desired skillsets with a battery of tests.

Congratulations! You are now the proud holder of Permanent Resident status in the Galilean Confederacy!

Go enjoy the trade discounts and private housing opportunities.

ENCEmbassyServicesBCERVisaFaction.strDesc:
Cost: $250,000

Immigrants can also fast-track their application through the Draft Service (DS) track. By materially contributing to the war effort, whether that be through mining, beacon-laying, or destruction of enemy materials, applicants can raise their clearance levels to become eligible as a Serviceman.

Those meeting the clearance requirements with sufficient funds have an option to apply for this status.

ENCEmbassyServicesBCERVisaFactionAccept.strDesc:
After submitting your application fee, a background check, and the a review of your material contributions, you are deemed an acceptable profile for admittance to DS.

Congratulations! You are now the proud holder of Permanent Resident status in the Galilean Confederacy!

Go enjoy the trade discounts and private housing opportunities.

ENCEmbassyServicesBCERVisaLocalSponsored.strDesc:
Cost: $500,000

The Heritage Sponsorship Program (HSP) in Galilean Confederacy is a component of Galilean Confederacy's immigration system, enabling Galilean Confederacy citizens and permanent residents to sponsor their spouses, family, or trusted friends for permanent residency in the Galilean Confederacy. The program aims to facilitate family reunification by allowing Galilean Confederacy citizens or permanent residents to bring their loved ones to live with them.

(Requires a Galilean Confederacy resident to agree to sponsor applicant first.)

After submitting your application fee, a background check, and the requisite interview of your sponsor, you are deemed an acceptable profile for admittance to HSP.

Congratulations! You are now the proud holder of Permanent Resident status in the Galilean Confederacy!

Go enjoy the trade discounts and private housing opportunities.

ENCEmbassyServicesBCERVisaCitAlready.strDesc:
Visa application services are only relevant to those who do not already have legal status in the Galilean Confederacy.

As a citizen of the Galilean Confederacy, you do not need this service.

ENCEmbassyServicesBCERVisaPRAlready.strDesc:
Visa application services are only relevant to those who do not already have legal status in the Galilean Confederacy.

As a permanent resident of the Galilean Confederacy, you do not need this service.

ENCMemoryFoliage.strTitle: Clobbered by a Memory of Foliage
ENCMemoryFoliage.strDesc:
An image of green flora, real flora, arrives to you from your past without warning. The plant was slick and glistening with dew, bedded in rich black soil, and home to more darting life in the form of gnats, mosquitos, and tiny spiders whose nearly invisible webs made them appear as if they were frozen in midair.

Merely a generation ago such a sight would mean almost nothing. One image among thousands collected during the course of normal living. But here, in the cold dead reaches of space, where the monotony of black nothing is broken only steel and plastic, the memory is as freighted with loss as it is enchanted by promise.

You find yourself wondering, quite earnestly, if you'll ever see such a thing again. Yes, there are places in The System where things still grow. But now that Earth is nothing but a broken promise, these places exist in an income bracket so far beyond your own that they are almost unheard of.

But they remain imaginable. And if there's one thing the corps can't kill, it is your spirit. So here you sit, imagining.

ENCMemoryFoliageDeeperClobber.strDesc: You do the difficult work of processing the harsh memory. While it causes you immediate emotional pain, it moves you closer to resolving the memory and its attendant traumas permanently. This kind of work, you're certain, will eventually yield deep emotional rewards.

ENCMemoryFoliageRevisit.strDesc: The difficult memory returns to you again uninvited. You can choose to suppress it, gaining a momentary respite from the fear it generates. Or you can do the difficult work of processing it, stirring up hard emotions in the present with the hope it might lead to permanent growth in the future.

ENCEmbassyServicesMSUZ.strDesc:
Most sovereignties in the System observe a tiered immigration status, or "strata." Usually ranging from undocumented (illegal) immigrant, up to full citizenship, a person's strata dictates which rights they enjoy with the sovereignty.

Rights can include access to certain areas or services, eligibility for private housing or ship docking, enhanced prices on trade authorization, or even legal protections or permissions.

Such rights are usually conferred by parents through birth (jus sanguinis), and in some cases, by being born in the territory (jus soli).

Obtaining legal status after birth usually involves applying for a visa, and may include getting a sponsor and/or paying a significant fee.

ENCMemoryProject.strTitle: Clobbered by a Memory of The Project You'll Never Finish
ENCMemoryProject.strDesc:
Later. Soonish. You'll get to it tomorrow, you tell yourself, when things slow down a little. When life stops happening to you and suddenly decides, for some reason you can't even imagine, to start respecting your to-do list.

Meanwhile your Big Project molders like a gargantuan river rock, wholly indifferent to the rushing currents of time splashing at its base. Every day of neglect creates new projects, new problems grown up from ignoring the first, each a creeping ivy, the mess so thick now that the initial rock is hardly visible.

You've lost track of the number of promises you've broken with yourself. At this point, you don't even have the energy to make another.

Now, in a moment of clarity borne on a wave of self disdain, you start to wonder if you're just not fit for the job.
