CeresP3TitanFinale1.strDesc: Someone is following you. The paranoia in Ceres space is rubbing off on you, or you might not have caught it. A silhouette drifts after you round every corner. You can see them distorted in the burnished walls; you snatch a glimpse when you pretend to consult your PDA for directions. Your shadow gets the fright of their life when you reach out from a pile of rugs (McArthur's Rugs For All Occasions And Surfaces!) and grab them by their shirt collar. They scream and holler, but they couldn't be more than four feet tall. You clip them across the chin and revolve them so they're facing you, unkempt hair flashing wildly. "What gives, kid?" The fresh spawn of Ceres' breeding vats, or brothels, scowls at you and tries to hunch into his jacket, so that he can shrink out of it and leave you holding an empty and grubby Extra Small. You clip him round the temple this time. "Stop that. Why are you following me? I won't ask again." "'Sposed to give ya a message, #$%#$," the child spits at you. "S'getoff me and lemme deliver." "Fine. A message. I'm going to let you go now," you say. "If my account's been skimmed after this I'm gonna space you and use your corpse for target practice. Copy?" He glowers at you, snot trailing from his nose. "If you hurt me the Rockefellas will hunt you down." "Yeah, to shake my hand and build me a statue." You plant the kid before you. "Talk.

CeresP3TitanFinale2.strDesc: The kid - who gives himself the unlikely name of 'Clay' - is a happy camper with a peach iced block and a gruel pouch to his name. It turns out he's to be both messenger and guide, and it seemed wise to build back some rapport. He's been leading you away and down from Port Mojave, skirting the main caverns of Calico and its offshoots, and through access tunnels long untravelled by humans. John Wayne wants you to meet someone. "And to prove it was him who said it, he said, 'tell [us-custom-characterGenderCond|his|her|their] sorry ass I'll dribble [us-custom-characterGenderCond|him|her|them] up and down a Breakout court if [us-custom-characterGenderCond|he doesn't|she doesn't|they don't] shut up and do what [us-custom-characterGenderCond|he's|she's|they're] told.'" It has plausibility on its side. "I grew up here," he says at one juncture, tossing aside the desiccated ice stick and starting on the gruel pouch. "Ceres? I figured." "No, dumbfuck," says Clay, and nods to the letters JS43a on the wall. "Here." He means this corridor. After plenty of walking and nearly companionable banter, you're beginning to wonder exactly where you're going and how long it will be. As you're about to demand this information from Clay, not for the first but certainly the last time, he gives a piercing whistle. "It's me! I've got the foreigner!" A pile of trash on the floor shudders and stands up. It's a woman holding a stub shotgun, and she is too close for comfort. "Ah," you say, nonplussed. She's wearing ghillie camouflage made from covering a standard pressure suit in sterilised (thankfully) garbage, empty cartons and plastic wrappers. She doesn't quite level the shotgun your way, but she doesn't look happy.

CeresP3TitanFinale3.strDesc:
"Are you the one I'm supposed to meet?" you say, polite as you can manage. She ignores you.

"You were supposed to clear this with the duty watch," she says to Clay curtly. "You set off fifteen earlybird alarms!"

"He promised me ten dollars on delivery," Clay says. "We had to change route cuz've Coalition patrols. S'not my fault." You didn't see any sign of patrols, but you've observed his uncanny sense of direction. If he says they were there, they probably were.

The trash-fighter slings her weapon over one shoulder, not happy about any of this. You swallow a sigh of relief, the only one feeling the tension. "You'll get your ten dollars once you're at the meet and not before," she says. "Someone has to go manually reset fifteen laser tripwires. Guess that's me." She stalks off the way you came.

Clay takes your hand and pulls you ahead. You reluctantly let yourself be pulled along. "What the hell are you getting me into? Who are these guys?"

"Duh," says Clay. He wrings the last drop out of his pouch and hands it to you empty. "This is the Revolution."

CeresP3TitanFinale4.strDesc:
One sheer wall of the cavern is a fifteen foot tall piece of fabric: Stars and Stripes forever, baby. The flag is pulled taut by guidewires. The red white and blue are faded, and there's a conspicuous oily-brown stain on the lower half, but other than that it's not hard to recognise. "What if someone wants to join who isn't American?" you ask John Wayne, who's idly spinning on one of those antique office chairs, which has been bolted to the floor.

"Simple," says John. "They can fuck off and start their own terrorist cell."

The cavern is oriented around the flag-wall, with banks of consoles facing it in rows. Some of the seats are occupied by Ceresian revolutionaries, an unremarkable group of men and women alike only in how much they radiate fatigue. All told, there are eight of you, including you and John Wayne.

"And all this old junk?" You nod to the consoles, too big to be modern.

"Some genius before our time decided it should look like NORAD," says John Wayne. "If you know what that is."

"I don't."

"Neither did they," he says, disgusted. "Except from movies."

CeresP3TitanFinale5.strDesc: "Why have you brought me here, John?" One of the revolutionaries clears her throat. "Yeah, I'd like to know that too." She's lounging against one of the consoles, arms crossed, blonde hair in a braid clipped to her back. A few loose strands wave in the microgravity. She's Korean-American, if you had to guess. "Since I'm supposed to be in command." "[us-firstname], meet Jane," says John. "Jane?" "Jane Fonda," says the woman icily. "He loves his stupid codenames." You look between the two of them. "John Wayne and Jane Fonda, okay," you say. "I think something's going over my head." "Yep!" says John happily. "Alright, listen up everyone! [us-firstname] here is going to help us win the war." Heads perk up at that, the first signs of life from the disgruntled militia you've seen. "[us-custom-characterGenderCond|He is?|She is?|They are?]" says Jane. "I am?" you echo her. "Yep!" repeats John. He picks up a remote from a console and points it at the flag. A long screen lowers across it, and he clicks through a display of briefing material.

CeresP3TitanFinale6.strDesc:
"This is what you've been preparing for," says John. "Months, years, of training, planning, waiting: it all comes down to this."

An image of an ageing Asian man appears on the screen. Black and white, poorly framed, tight background and obscured foreground customary of a telephoto spy lens. He has a perennially unfashionable straight fringed hairstyle.

"This is Ben Choong," says John. "The captain here has been scouring Ceres high and low for him. Even asked yours truly about it. Well, Ben knew me. Knew far more than anyone 'round here should. Maybe that's why a couple weeks ago he went missing."

Security camera footage, grainy and stuttering along frame by frame, of a hallway familiar to you: the entrance to Choong's apartment on Ring Station. Four people in bulky clothes line up outside the door, faces obscured by unknown means, green squares drawn by the security system in an abortive attempt to ID them. Rather than guns, they prepare long telescoping batons. One of them kicks in the door. The group files inside, professionally swift.

"That's him getting his head kicked in by God-knows-who," John says, winking at you. "Don't say I do nothin' for ya."

CeresP3TitanFinale7.strDesc: The assailants come back out the door dragging a body between two of them, arms linked under his shoulders. The camera's ID software enthusiastically identifies him as B. Choong. It isolates and enlarging the area within the green square overlay - face bloody, mouth agape, head lolling to one side - and pastes a transcript of his Ceres worker's license beside it. "I asked around," says John, "and I'm the kinda guy when I ask, people answer." His self-satisfied tone slips. "Ordinarily, that is. Not for this man. Nobody's sayin' shit. Wasted my good thumbscrews." He moves to the next slide. Ring Station from five klicks out. A camera from the ship's bow. Front and centre: the biggest ship docked to the Ring, a warship of exorbitant tonnage. "This is the Yangtze-3," he says. "Our big beautiful bitch in the sky. We've been trying," he says to you, for your benefit, "to flip someone higher than a midshipman for months now. No dice. Credit to the Martians, they know when to close ranks. 'Cept they fucked up, cos our Food Services guy confirmed it. They got a Lunar national on board. Got some special dietary needs. I reckon that's our guy."

ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoBeg.strDesc: "Please don't kill me," you say fervently. "I really, really, really don't want to die, and not like this, not over some accident." "Not like this?" he repeats, incensed. "It would be an honour to die by my hand. I've sent four souls to Hell. Wish you to join them?" Christ, now he's talking like a Shakespeare villain. "No, no sir," you say smartly. Outside the tunnel vision you've fixed on this psychopathic teen brandishing a museum piece, you can sense the flow of street traffic ignoring the street drama with uncanny propriety. "I wish not to dishonour you by wasting your bullet on worthless offworld trash like myself." He cocks his head. "That wasn't half bad, in truth." One of his lackeys nods sincerely. "Okay. I'll spare your miserable life. But maybe I'll put one arm out of commission, so you don't forget." He takes aim, his gun hand drifting lazily down to target your shoulder.

ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoAuntLiz.strDesc:
"CHADWICK O'NEILL," bellows a woman's voice from above. The tall youth - Chadwick - cringes at once, and the gun is no longer pointed at you. You release a breath you didn't know you'd held.

A short older woman - though she couldn't be much past forty - swoops down like an angel. She plants herself in front of Chadwick, who can't meet her look. His friends begin drifting away in ones and twos. "What would your mother say if she saw you mistreating this clumsy foreigner? What about your father, Heaven rest his soul?"

"It wasn't like that, Aunt Liz," Chadwick says to the ground. "I was only -"

Aunt Liz smacks him backhand across the face. It's not for show. She's wearing rings. Blood spirals away toward the city lights. She hits him again exactly as hard. When he raises his head, he already has a bruise. His murderous exterior is shattered, and a frightened child peers through it.

"Go to your room," she says. Quietly said, but somehow the entire street will have heard it. Chadwick backs up as fast as he can, flipping and shooting off on his gas jets without any of his former grace.

Aunt Liz - presumably Liz, to you - drifts over to her second priority. "Thank you," you say. "I don't know what I did, but -"

"Silence, Offworld," she says. There's no venom to it, but it's much more cutting than when her nephew said it. "I am speaking. If you do not have one, buy a gun and carry it openly. Without it you will invite random violence, or unwanted sexual attention."

"Are you serious?" you say.

"Yes," she says. "It would be best for you to handle your business here, and depart from Calico as soon as you are able."

She turns on one heel jet and leaves.

ENCFirstDockBCRSInfoAskCalico.strTitle: Ask about Ceres and Calico City
ENCFirstDockBCRSInfoAskCalico.strDesc:
"Calico City is kind of a crazy place, right?" you say.

"What do you expect? An American colony abandoned by its creditors long ago; then along comes Xinhua." She shrugs. "Isolated, xenophobic, kept in arrested development by a foreign superpower, desperately clutching to their myths of a glorious past - all things considered, and taking the long view, they're quite a normal people. They've been taught to worship a way of life that never was ..." 

She lingers on the thought, then plows on a little more brusquely. "Fucked up is normal, on this world stage of ours." She leans forward and whispers a secret to you. "The hot springs are divine. Cryovolcanic mineral water is very good for the skin."

"I'll have to check those out," you say.

"Mm, well, make sure you're armed at all times. They like their cowboy movies. If you offend someone -" she cocks a finger-pistol at you. "Pew! Pew, pew!" 

Perhaps some people never get the hang of onomatopoeia.

ENCFirstDockBCRSInfoAskGalCon.strDesc:
"What's the story with the Galilean Confederacy?"

"Oof, where to begin," she says. "You know about Troy-Jupiter, all that?"

"Kind of," you say.

"You might've seen them in the headlines a few years back. The Troy-Jupiter Group. Local oligarchs of Jupiter; most of it, anyway, twenty moons' worth. A cautionary tale," she wags a finger, "on how much one may starve the serfdom before they do something about it."

"Food was that scarce?" you say doubtfully.

"Of course it wasn't," she says. She smiles. "Not really, anyway. A few shipments went missing that really ought to have made it there. Regardless, who do you think was first on half rations?"

"The executives and their families, as a way of gracefully admitting fault," you say. Eleni snorts. "Probably law enforcement too, to show solidarity."

"The latter actually happened," she says, "and that's how we got the Galilean Confederacy, and why Troy-Jupiter is no more."

ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoHoldYourGround.strDesc:
"I'm not apologising for anything," you say. "You ran into me. I saw the whole thing - I was there."

He draws the piece. "I have to burn this shirt," he says thoughtfully. "Because it got Offworld sweat on it, or it got Offworld blood on it." He levels it at you. "The choice is yours. Beg, Offworld."

ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoCarrying.strDesc:
You let your hand drift to your armament, too.

"If I made a mistake, it won't be me who pays for it," you say evenly. "Your friends look like adults." A harmless untruth. "If they're injured, they can speak for themselves."

You lock eyes. It's not hard to get the measure of him. He needs to save face, and if you back down, he can't. He breaks his gaze first. He grins boyishly at his crew, who look none the worse for wear.

"I think we're good here," he says. Suddenly he's friendly, even charming. "Welcome to Calico, friend. We hope you enjoy your visit."

They retreat in good order. Nobody on the street has batted an eyelid.

What the hell is wrong with this place?

ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoBegIronically.strDesc: "Sure, I can do this," you say. "Do you guys lick boots here? Where do you stand on boots?" A vein pulses in his forehead. "Okay, not that. How about this: I'll make it up to you. Call your mother. I'll take her out to dinner. Treat her right, pay for everything, eat her box, call her in the morning." Damn, whispers one of the posse, in reverence or disgust. You spread your hands. "Well? Where's my bullet, guy? I've got somewhere to be." Tears forming at the corner of his eyes, he lowers the gun. He drifts away, shoulders hunched. One of the girls swoops after him, concerned. Dollars to donuts, that thing was a replica. Or unloaded. You look at his retreating back, annoyed as you are mystified. One of his friends passes you, reproachful look on his face. "Not cool," he says. "Chad's going through a tough time right now." You nod, nonplussed. To reply would be a waste of effort.

InspectBraincase2.strDesc:
You don the cybernetic accoutrements and adopt a relaxed posture.

Slowly the ambient noise of the ship is replaced by the white noise of the wind and snow.

Dr. Choong looks up from a book. "Ah, [us-surname]. Back to see me. Where did we leave things last?"

ChoongLibrary.strTitle: Ask him about the media library
ChoongLibrary.strDesc: "Watch anything good while you've been stuck in here?" you ask. "What kind of setup have they got?" "Mm," he grunts. His face glazes over, his grin turning glassy. "All the screen libraries are empty," he says. "Someone's little joke at my expense. All save one entry." "Which is?" "An Old Earth classic. The Prisoner, 1967," he says. His leaden voice betrays a cloying familiarity with the property. "Cute," you say. "I could add some from my ship's archive, if you like." He picks up an Earth style paperback book from the coffee table and waves it. "I'm well stocked, I assure you. It took an adjustment period, in which I watched The Prisoner 163 times, but I'm finally back into literary fiction."

ChoongLibrary_1.strDesc: "What's it about?" "The Prisoner?" asks Choong. "Not sure, really. Ostensibly it's about one man they call Number 6, a spy with a spotty past. He's kept by his own people in a planned prison town for spies, because he knows secrets too dangerous to let him retire." "Do you play as him?" you ask. "Or are you the warden trying to stop him from getting out?" "They were still working on interactive elements in 1967, so you watch him try and fail to escape each week," he says, smiling. "But the boundaries of the prison are inscrutable. There are no walls, and every time he thinks he's made it back to his old life, they seem to snap their fingers and he returns to the same miserable little town." "That's painfully on the nose," you say. "They must have been proud of coming up with that one." He sighs. "Nobody forced me to watch it, at least," he says. "That was my own stubborn self."

ChoongPlateau2_Exit.strDesc:
Choong doesn't look pleased, but he doesn't seem possessed of the will to do anything about it.

"I've hit a nerve," you say. "Would you like me to come back another time?"

"Come back whenever you damn well please," he says. "Or carry on talking. It doesn't matter to me."

ChoongTakeBreak2.strTitle: Come back when you damn well please
ChoongTakeBreak2.strDesc:
You slowly strip off the Renbao rig and blink away the stale air.

Things aren't exactly going well, but by that same token, it would be hard to imagine what constitutes 'going well'.

InspectBraincase3.strDesc:
You don the cybernetic accoutrements and adopt a relaxed posture.

Slowly the ambient noise of the ship is replaced by the white noise of the wind and snow.

Dr. Choong looks up from a book. "Ah, [us-surname]. Back to see me. Where did we leave things last?"

AVClub_The_Return_2.strDesc:
The dorm is full of an electric heat; the AC is cracking along in double time trying to keep up with a dozen warm bodies. You're crowded the moment you enter by fans eager to see the tape. "Holy shit, it's the newbie! / Do you have it? / What's on it?"

Smiley cuts through the crowd and drags you centre stage. "Back off! This is the [us-custom-characterGenderCond|man|woman|hero] of the hour. Let'em breathe."

The simple act of passing off the drive with the video on it takes on an unavoidable degree of ceremony. A satisfied hush sweeps through the club as Smiley slots the drive into his PDA. He navigates to the file and hovers on its selection. "Before we begin," he says, "libations."

You'd noticed that most of the group have e-cigs or hand rolled cigarettes close by. Now they all have one or the other in hand, and are eagerly smoking away. A tall man you'd hazard a guess is Abacho hands you a little black weed pen. "Trust me," he says, "this is once in a lifetime."

"What's in it?" you ask.

"Marijuana," he says, and winks.

AVClub_The_Return_Smoke.strDesc:
You shrug and take hit on the pen. You expect to cough, but it's incredibly smooth, and the taste is sweet, nothing like the harsh green bite of MJ.

You cough anyway as an experiment, look between the pen and Abacho. "There's no way in hell this is weed. What is it really?"

"It's home grown," he insists. "It tastes better, doesn't it?"

You flick the pen back. It oscillates over to him. "It should taste like weed, if that's what it is. Stay away from me, man."

AVClub_The_Return_DontSmoke.strDesc:
"Thanks, but no," you say. "That's what the party actually's about? Just getting high? No offence, but that's like every third dorm on K-LEG."

Abacho tries to look offended while trying not to burn his fingers on the roach. "We're all about the kino. You'll see."

AVClub_The_Return_Watch.strDesc:
The player begins. Nothing, at first, happens.

Smiley looks at you, unaccountably nervous, as if you've messed something up.

"Come to me," says a voice. The room jumps. Someone yelps, and another laughs at their fright.

"Who said that?" says one of the Mollys, and everyone shushes her.

"Come to me," says the voice. Androgynous, toneless, soft but resonant in this small space. At the corners of the image, arcs of white appear. You're looking into the black sun as you drift away.

"Come to me," it says.

"Rule of threes," says someone knowingly. "Yeah, I'll be right there!" says another.

The player pauses. Everyone yells at Smiley, his hand on the PDA. He raises a hand for calm. "No more talking! This is a first watch! No talking!"

The room calms. Molly Liu looks as if she's seen a ghost. Abacho struggles to keep his eyes open as he hits the pen for the umpteenth time. Smiley presses play.

AVClub_The_Return_Watch_1.strDesc: "- for many peoples, these were the first gods. And the greatest of the deities, the king of all gods, Jupiter." The footage is being filmed surreptitiously from a desk, looking down on an amphitheatre to a lecturer in mid-ramble. Cut: A garland, white flowers linked with gold lace, is laid upon a dark haired youth. An unseen voice asks a question, and the youth replies. Blocky yellow subtitles translate it from Russian, or a similar Slavic tongue. Subtitles: "How're you feeling?" / "I'm okay." The youth smiles. Her eyes are bright gold. Cut: "What about the Vestal Virgins? They were sacrificed." A student close by lowers his hand, looking smug. "They were killed for a crime. Capital punishment. Very common, still practised today. Human sacrifice is a colonial invention," says the lecturer, "libel by Conquistadors to justify the invasion. You can do anything to someone you believe is demonic." Cut: A low voice drones. The garlanded youth floats down a steel accessway, white tassels streaming behind her. Men and women in conventional pressure suits follow and precede her, some kind of honour guard. The suits are adorned with colourful patchwork heraldry, strong reds and blues. A second voice, then a third, joins the droning in perfect fifths. More voices begin a contrapuntal melody. The melody is full of vibrato, verging on quarter tones. It must be a folk tradition, though one you've not heard. They pass through a bulkhead into a wide cargo hold. The youth dives into it. The honour guard fans around her, singing. On the other side of the hold, the sarcophagus. Cut: The dialogue continues. "But wasn't human sacrifice witnessed by the colonists? How is it libel if it actually happened?" "The scholarship is shockingly poor on the subject." The lecturer is replaced by an upside down view of the documentarian's face, right up his nostrils. He's a young Xinhuan or Malaysian man, and he scratches his nose, bored. "I think it's more likely they witnessed cultural practices alien to them, which they misinterpreted in a way convenient to them." Cut: The singing has stopped, save for one voice, which carries the melody as the youth floats into the open sarcophagus. She climbs inside, a solemn expression on her face. The singer closes the lid. Surrounding the sarcophagus is a network of coiled tubing and steel cylinders. The honour guard gathers at a central console, all except the singer, who kneels at the side of the sarcophagus. Pneumatic hissing from the cylinders. The singer halts his song, and taps twice on the lid. A singular dull thud comes from inside. The singer flashes the thumbs up to those at the console. In unison, they break back into song. Once again, the playback pauses, cutting the singing short. The uproar from the club is even more venomous but once again Smiley calls for quiet, waving urgently. "Listen! Can you hear that?"

AVClub_The_Return_Listen.strDesc: Far in the distance, a plaintive voice cries: "Zhou? Where are you? Zhou?" It's a cry well known on K-LEG. Less common, maybe, on the Flotilla. AyoSec are inbound. "It's a sweep!" The room explodes into chaos. A handful run for the door. Whether or not they're coming for this group, it's best not to stick around to find out. You've got maybe thirty seconds to act.

AVClub_The_Return_Cops_MakeBreak.strTitle: Make a break for it with the crowd
AVClub_The_Return_Cops_MakeBreak.strDesc:
Whatever's on that tape isn't worth tangling with the law. You bolt for the exit, reaching it just ahead of the others.

Seconds later, you're outside, into the passageway. You have to throw yourself to one side to avoid an old spacer hurtling toward you.

A steady human tide racing helter-skelter pulls you away from the main access routes.
